# Starter Kit documentation (/)



The kit puts an Exasol database on this computer and sets it up for the work you do. What it sets up depends on your **persona**. Pick a section below, or in the list at the top of the sidebar.

<Cards>
  <Card title="All personas" href="/kit">
    The kit itself: what a persona is, loading data, column maps, add-ons and every command.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Data Scientist" href="/data-scientist">
    Four notebooks and nine steps: load data, agree what each column means, explore, model, ask questions and share.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## From a notebook [#from-a-notebook]

```python
import exakit.nb as nb

nb.docs()                  # your persona's section, under the cell
nb.docs("descriptor")      # search
nb.docs(nb.describe)       # one command's page
```

`nb.docs()` opens the section of the persona whose notebook you are in.


# The kit and its personas (/kit)



The Exasol Personal Local Starter Kit installs a database on this computer and the tools around it. One command, `exakit`, runs all of it.

## What every install has [#what-every-install-has]

| Part          | What it is for                                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The database  | Exasol, running on this computer                              |
| `exakit`      | The command that starts, checks, loads and updates everything |
| The AI bridge | Lets your AI clients query the database, read-only            |
| AI skills     | Instructions that teach an AI client how to use the kit       |
| Sample data   | Datasets to practise on                                       |

## What a persona adds [#what-a-persona-adds]

A **persona** is the kit set up for one kind of work. It decides which datasets are loaded, which add-ons are installed and which notebooks you get. See [What is a persona](/kit/personas/what-is-a-persona).

## Find your task [#find-your-task]

| I want to                                             | Go to                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| See or change which persona this kit is               | [Choose and change a persona](/kit/personas/choose-and-change) |
| Load a file, a folder or a kit dataset                | [Load data](/kit/data/load-data)                               |
| Say what each column of a table means                 | [Column maps](/kit/data/column-maps)                           |
| Run a query from the terminal                         | [Run SQL](/kit/data/run-sql)                                   |
| Install a dashboard server, notebooks or another tool | [Add-ons](/kit/tools/add-ons)                                  |
| Open JupyterLab or Marimo                             | [Notebooks](/kit/tools/notebooks)                              |
| See what a piece of work did, step by step            | [Workflows](/kit/tools/workflows)                              |
| Connect an AI client                                  | [AI clients and skills](/kit/tools/ai-clients-and-skills)      |
| Look up a command                                     | [All exakit commands](/kit/reference/commands)                 |
| Work through the Data Scientist notebooks             | [Data Scientist](/data-scientist)                              |

## Help on this computer [#help-on-this-computer]

```bash
exakit help                # every command
exakit help data-load      # one command in full
exakit catalog load        # search the commands
exakit status              # is the database up?
```

The same help is built into the kit, so it always matches the version you have.


# Add-ons and downloads (/security/add-ons-and-downloads)



The kit pins what it downloads. Each pin is a version in `versions.json`, and where the kit can check the file, a SHA-256 digest. The download is checked before anything is unpacked, and a file that fails the check is removed.

## What is pinned, and how [#what-is-pinned-and-how]

Every pin is in `versions.json` at the root of the repository. The kit reads the copy that shipped with it, not a copy fetched from the network. Each module says so in a comment, for example "The kit copy's own pin, never the fetched document (SEC-13)" in `setup/lib/exapump.sh`.

| Item                                  | Version pinned | SHA-256 pinned                             | Where the check is                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Semantic Views (`semantic-views`)     | Yes            | Yes, for the archive                       | `_download()` and `_unpack()` in `marketplace/addons/semantic_views.py`                                                                          |
| Exasol Scheduler (`exasol-scheduler`) | Yes            | Yes, per platform                          | `_download()` in `marketplace/addons/exasol_scheduler.py`                                                                                        |
| Exasol for VS Code (`exasol-vscode`)  | Yes            | Yes, for the VSIX                          | `install()` in `marketplace/addons/exasol_vscode.py`, after the download                                                                         |
| JSON Tables (`json-tables`)           | Yes            | Yes, for the wheel and the platform assets | `_asset()` in `marketplace/addons/json_tables.py`                                                                                                |
| UDF devkit (`udf-devkit`)             | Yes            | Yes, for each container, with its size     | `verify()` and `fetch()` in `marketplace/udf_container.py`                                                                                       |
| exapump                               | Yes            | Yes, per platform                          | `exapump_expected_sha256()` in `setup/lib/exapump.sh`                                                                                            |
| uv                                    | Yes            | Yes, per platform                          | `exakit_uv_pinned_sha256()` and `exakit_uv_install_pinned()` in `setup/lib/common.sh`; `Install-ExakitUvPinned` in `setup/lib/exakit-common.ps1` |
| Dash Server (`dash-server`)           | Yes            | No                                         | Installed with `uv pip install` of the pinned release URL, in `marketplace/addons/dash_server.py`                                                |
| dbt-exasol, pyexasol, notebook        | Yes            | No                                         | Version only, in `versions.json`                                                                                                                 |

## The order of checks [#the-order-of-checks]

For the archive-based add-ons, the code follows the same order. Semantic Views is the clearest example:

1. `_expected_digest()` takes the digest from the kit's own pin, when the version matches. Otherwise it reads the release's `.sha256` file.
2. `_download()` streams the archive to disk and computes its SHA-256 as it writes. It compares the digest with the expected one. On a mismatch it raises `Checksum mismatch` and deletes the archive.
3. Only then does `_unpack()` run. It refuses any archive entry whose resolved path is outside the destination folder (`the Semantic Views archive holds a path outside its folder`). It also requires `tools/install.py` and at least one `build/install/*.sql` file.

The UDF containers follow the same pattern. `fetch()` in `marketplace/udf_container.py` downloads to a temporary `.part` file, and `verify()` checks the size and the SHA-256 before the file is moved into the cache. A cached file is verified again when it is used, and removed if it fails. The mirror setting, `EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINERS_MIRROR`, changes where the file comes from, not whether it is checked.

Downloads must use `https://`. `_https()` in `marketplace/addons/semantic_views.py` refuses any other scheme and refuses a redirect that leaves HTTPS. The UDF path checks the redirect the same way.

## Where a digest comes from when the pin does not match [#where-a-digest-comes-from-when-the-pin-does-not-match]

A pin is used only when the requested version is the pinned one. For other versions, the code can take the digest from the release itself:

* Semantic Views reads the release's own `.sha256` file.
* Exasol Scheduler's `_digest()` reads the release's `.sha256` file, and then the release API.
* exapump's `exapump_expected_sha256()` falls back to a digest in the release API.

These digests come from the same host as the file. They confirm that the download matches what that release says. They do not confirm that the release is one the kit's maintainers reviewed. Only the `versions.json` pin does that.

## Escape hatches [#escape-hatches]

Three add-ons can install without a checksum when you set an environment variable to `1`. Without the variable, a missing checksum is refused.

| Add-on             | Variable                                   | What it does                                                                                   | Where                                                     |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Exasol for VS Code | `EXAKIT_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_EXASOL_VSCODE`    | Installs the VSIX with no digest                                                               | `marketplace/addons/exasol_vscode.py`                     |
| Exasol Scheduler   | `EXAKIT_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_EXASOL_SCHEDULER` | Installs the archive with no digest                                                            | `_download()` in `marketplace/addons/exasol_scheduler.py` |
| JSON Tables        | `EXAKIT_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_JSON_TABLES`      | Installs the asset with no digest. The error message says "a maintainer may explicitly set" it | `_asset()` in `marketplace/addons/json_tables.py`         |

Do not set these for a normal install. A setting left in your shell applies to every later install.

## Skills are copied byte for byte [#skills-are-copied-byte-for-byte]

The AI skills the kit ships from other repositories are copies of upstream files. The list is in `skills/upstream.json`, with the repository, a pinned commit or tag, and the path. `tools/sync_upstream_skills.py` writes `skills/upstream.lock.json`, which records a commit and a SHA-256 for every file, and each copy's license file. The script's `--check` mode fails when a copy differs from the lock, or when a pin falls behind the version the kit installs. The repository's notes say the copies are never edited by hand, and `tests/skills.sh` checks them against the lock.

## Add-ons the kit did not install [#add-ons-the-kit-did-not-install]

The kit leaves an installation it did not make alone:

* `system_present()` in `marketplace/addons/dash_server.py` treats a `dash-server` command on your PATH as managed outside the kit when the kit has no receipt for it. The kit never installs over it, updates it or removes it.
* `marketplace/addons/exasol_vscode.py` says: "A user-installed extension remains the user's installation." It is listed as managed outside the kit and never offered again.

## Removing an add-on [#removing-an-add-on]

```bash
exakit uninstall dash-server --dry-run    # print what would be removed, change nothing
exakit uninstall dash-server --yes        # remove that one add-on
exakit uninstall --dry-run                # the full plan
```

`setup/help/exakit.json` says `--dry-run` "previews the full plan and changes nothing". The full uninstall keeps uv and the PATH line in your shell profile, because uv may be used by other tools and the profile line is shared (the comment above `exakit_uninstall_run()` in `setup/lib/common.sh`).

## Logs [#logs]

Each add-on's output goes to `logs/marketplace.log` in the kit home, created at mode 600. `run_logged()` in `marketplace/runtime.py` replaces the values of any environment variable whose name ends in `PASSWORD`, `TOKEN`, `_KEY` or `SECRET` before the output is written.

## Limits [#limits]

* Dash Server, dbt-exasol, pyexasol and the notebook package are pinned by version only. The kit checks no digest for them.
* Three add-ons have an escape hatch that installs without a digest.
* Digests taken from a release, rather than from `versions.json`, check the download against that release only.
* The checks are SHA-256 digests. The add-on modules in `marketplace/` contain no signature verification.


# AI clients and the read-only user (/security/ai-clients)



AI clients never connect as the admin. The kit creates a second database user, `mcp_readonly` (the default of `EXAKIT_MCP_READONLY_USER`, set in `setup/lib/common.sh`), and the Exasol MCP server connects as that user. The server runs beside the database, on 127.0.0.1, by default on port 4896 (`EXAKIT_MCP_SIDECAR_PORT`).

## Who connects as whom [#who-connects-as-whom]

The launcher starts the Exasol MCP server as a sidecar. Its own default connects it as the admin. The kit's comment in `setup/lib/mcp.sh` says so: "the launcher connects it as SYS ... the kit connects it as its read-only MCP user." `_mcp_sidecar_definition()` in the same file writes the kit's definition, with `EXA_USER` set to the read-only user and `EXA_PASSWORD` read from `mcp_readonly_password`.

```text
You -> AI client -> Exasol MCP server (127.0.0.1:4896) -> database, as mcp_readonly
You -> exakit sql -> database, as the admin profile (not sandboxed; see Limits)
```

## What the read-only user may do [#what-the-read-only-user-may-do]

`exakit_configure_mcp_readonly_access()` in `setup/lib/common.sh` grants exactly three system privileges and then checks that nothing else is held:

* `CREATE SESSION`, so it can connect.
* `USE ANY SCHEMA`, so it can see every schema.
* `SELECT ANY TABLE`, so it can read every table and view, including ones created later.

The grant comment says `SELECT ANY DICTIONARY` is deliberately not granted, so system dictionaries stay private. `_exakit_assert_mcp_readonly_posture()` checks that the user holds those three and no other system privilege, directly, through a role, or as an object grant. It also runs a write probe that must be rejected. The install stops if any check fails.

The read-only user's default schema is `STARTER_KIT` (`EXAKIT_MCP_READONLY_SCHEMAS`). It is only the landing schema for local uploads. It does not limit what the user may read.

## What the server allows [#what-the-server-allows]

`_mcp_sidecar_definition()` in `setup/lib/mcp.sh` sets these server settings:

| Setting                     | Value   |
| --------------------------- | ------- |
| `enable_read_query`         | `true`  |
| `enable_write_query`        | `false` |
| `enable_preprocessor_tools` | `false` |
| `enable_read_bucketfs`      | `false` |
| `enable_write_bucketfs`     | `false` |
| `default_row_limit`         | `1000`  |

These are the server's own switches. The database's grants are the real limit. A client that sends a write is refused by the database, because the user has no write privilege.

<Callout type="warn">
  `SELECT ANY TABLE` means an AI client can read every column of every table, including columns that hold personal data. The sensitive-column rule in [What is sent to an AI model](/security/what-goes-to-a-model) limits what the kit's helpers send to a model. It does not limit what the MCP user can read.
</Callout>

## The server has no token [#the-server-has-no-token]

The sidecar runs with `--no-auth` on 127.0.0.1 (`args` in `_mcp_sidecar_definition()`). The kit also sets `FASTMCP_HTTP_HOST_ORIGIN_PROTECTION` to `true`. This repository does not document what that setting blocks beyond its name. Any program on this computer that can reach port 4896 can call the server, and the server answers with whatever the read-only user may read.

## How a notebook question is approved [#how-a-notebook-question-is-approved]

A notebook never runs SQL it has not shown you. The steps are in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/ask.py`:

1. `ask()` drafts one SQL statement from the approved column map. Nothing runs.
2. You read the SQL. `Proposal.approve()` records its SHA-256 digest and writes an `ASK_APPROVE` line to the workflow log with the SQL text.
3. `Proposal.edit()` replaces the SQL and clears the approval.
4. `Proposal.run()` computes the digest of the text it is about to run. If it differs from the approved digest, it raises `This SQL has not been approved`.
5. `_read_sql()` accepts text that starts with `SELECT` or `WITH` and has no semicolon before the end. This is a shape check. It is not a SQL parser. The database user and the server settings above are the real limit.
6. `_mcp_settings()` refuses to run unless the connection user is not the admin, the password file is `mcp_readonly_password`, `connection.validated` is `true`, and the server URL is loopback `http`. The notebook sends no password. The sidecar holds the read-only login.

```python
proposal = ask(ds, "How many orders were cancelled per category?")
print(proposal)          # the SQL, one clause per line, not yet approved
proposal.approve()       # records the digest of this exact text
result = proposal.run()  # refuses if the SQL changed after approval
```

The approval is per SQL text. It is not per session and not per question. The workflow log keeps the statement text, its digest and the row count.

## What the admin can do from the terminal [#what-the-admin-can-do-from-the-terminal]

`exakit sql` runs as the admin. Its help entry in `setup/help/exakit.json` says so in its warning: "This connects with the starter-kit profile, which is the ADMIN user and is NOT sandboxed. The read-only boundary is the MCP user, not this command." `exakit sql --write` runs writes as the admin. Use the read-only path for anything an AI client or an untrusted script should run.

## Limits [#limits]

* The MCP server has no authentication token. Its protection is the loopback address and the read-only user.
* The read-only user reads every table, so an AI client can query personal-data columns the kit would not send to a model.
* `_read_sql()` checks the shape of the text. It does not parse SQL. A statement that passes the shape check still runs as the read-only user, so the database decides what it may do.
* `exakit sql` is not read-only and not sandboxed.
* The read-only user's password is kept in the credentials folder (see [Credentials](/security/credentials)).


# Credentials and passwords (/security/credentials)



The kit holds three kinds of secret: the database admin password (the SYS user), the password of the read-only user that AI clients use, and any model or Langfuse key you give the notebooks. Each secret is a file in one folder, `~/.exasol-starter-kit/credentials/`. A password is never written to `exakit.env`, and the manifest records the path of each credential file, not the password.

## Where they live [#where-they-live]

| File under `credentials/`                                                                 | What it holds                                                                                            | Written by                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `runtime_sys_password`                                                                    | The database admin (SYS) password. Its path is recorded as `runtime.password_file` in the kit's manifest | `store_credential` in `setup/lib/common.sh`, called from `setup/lib/exapump.sh` and `exakit_configure_mcp_readonly_access` |
| `mcp_readonly_password`                                                                   | The password of the read-only MCP user                                                                   | `store_credential` in `exakit_configure_mcp_readonly_access`, `setup/lib/common.sh`                                        |
| `notebook_store_master_password`                                                          | The master password of the notebook connection store                                                     | `_credential()` in `marketplace/addons/notebook.py`                                                                        |
| `notebook_model_api_key`, `notebook_langfuse_secret_key` and the other `notebook_*` files | A model or Langfuse key, only if you asked for `remember=True`                                           | `_write_private()` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/setup_env.py`                                                            |

Two more files hold a password in a different form:

* `~/.exapump/config.toml` (the exapump profile) holds the admin password as a TOML value. `exapump_write_profile()` in `setup/lib/exapump.sh` writes it, then runs `chmod 600`.
* The launcher's `sidecars.yaml` holds a reference to `mcp_readonly_password`, not the password. The file is written with mode 0600. `_mcp_sidecar_definition()` in `setup/lib/mcp.sh` says: "The password is a file reference the editor resolves; it is never in this text."

### File permissions [#file-permissions]

* The credentials folder is set to `700` by `store_credential()`. Each file is written as `<name>.tmp`, set to `600`, then renamed into place. An interrupted run cannot leave a truncated secret.
* `_exakit_warn_unprotected_credentials()` checks that `600` took effect. On a filesystem that ignores Unix modes, such as a Windows drive mounted into WSL, the kit prints a warning once per run.
* On Windows, `Protect-ExakitFile()` in `setup/lib/exakit-common.ps1` removes inherited permissions and grants full control to the current user only.
* Generated passwords are 24 characters of `A-Z`, `a-z` and `0-9`. `generate_password()` in `setup/lib/common.sh` reads `/dev/urandom`. `New-ExakitPassword()` in `setup/lib/exakit-common.ps1` uses `RandomNumberGenerator`.

## How a password reaches a tool [#how-a-password-reaches-a-tool]

| Tool                                                                        | How the password travels                                                                                                                                                 | Where to check it                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| exapump, for the profile                                                    | The password goes in the environment variable `EXAKIT_PROFILE_PASSWORD`, read by a Python writer. It is never in argv                                                    | `exapump_write_profile()`, `setup/lib/exapump.sh`                                          |
| exapump, for SQL that contains a password (`CREATE USER ... IDENTIFIED BY`) | The SQL goes to exapump on standard input                                                                                                                                | `_exakit_run_exapump_sql()`, `setup/lib/common.sh`                                         |
| The read-only user's temporary config                                       | The admin and read-only passwords go in `EXAKIT_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `EXAKIT_READONLY_PASSWORD`. The temporary file comes from `mktemp` and is removed on exit or failure | `_exakit_write_exapump_config()` and `exakit_track_sensitive_tmp()`, `setup/lib/common.sh` |
| The Exasol MCP server                                                       | The definition names the file, `EXA_PASSWORD` with a `valueFile`. The launcher reads the file                                                                            | `_mcp_sidecar_definition()`, `setup/lib/mcp.sh`                                            |
| The notebook connection store                                               | The master password is read from its file and passed as `SCS_MASTER_PASSWORD` to the store tool                                                                          | `marketplace/addons/notebook.py`, around the `SCS_MASTER_PASSWORD` line                    |
| A source's password (virtual schemas)                                       | You type or paste it. It goes to the engine on standard input. A key from a file goes to `paste.secret` at mode 600, which is deleted after use                          | `_exakit_vs_tui_paste()`, `setup/lib/virtual-schemas.sh`                                   |

A child process's environment is readable by its owner and by root, not by other users. The kit's comments rely on that. Each variable is unset again after the call that needs it.

### Where a source password ends up [#where-a-source-password-ends-up]

For a virtual schema the engine runs `CREATE CONNECTION ... TO <url> USER <user> IDENTIFIED BY <secret>` (`create_connection()` in `setup/virtual-schemas/engine/lifecycle.py`). The password is therefore stored in the database, in the CONNECTION object. The kit does not check how the database stores that object. See the [CREATE CONNECTION reference](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/sql/create_connection.htm) for the syntax.

## What stays out of logs [#what-stays-out-of-logs]

* The installer log is created at mode 600 (`setup/lib/common.sh`, the `EXAKIT_LOG_FILE` block).
* `_exakit_redact_mcp_secret_output()` in `setup/lib/common.sh` replaces the password, and the value after `IDENTIFIED BY`, before any `CREATE USER` or `ALTER USER` output is logged or shown.
* `run_logged()` in `marketplace/runtime.py` replaces the value of every child environment variable whose name ends in `PASSWORD`, `TOKEN`, `_KEY` or `SECRET` with `[redacted]`. The marketplace log is set to mode 600.
* `setup/lib/envfile.sh` refuses a settings-file name that contains `PASSWORD`, `API_KEY`, `TOKEN` or `SECRET`. A secret cannot come from `exakit.env`.
* `ModelConfig` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/model_config.py` declares the key with `field(repr=False)`. `redact_secrets()` removes the key and custom header values in plain, URL-encoded and base64 forms, and whatever follows `Authorization`, `Bearer`, `Basic` or an `api-key` label.
* `notebook/package/exakit_nb/workflow.py` refuses a log payload whose key is named like a secret, or whose DSN contains a password. A statement that mentions `IDENTIFIED BY`, `PASSWORD` or `API_KEY` is logged as `<redacted: credential-like SQL>`.
* `setup_env.use_model()` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/setup_env.py` asks for a key with a hidden prompt. The key stays in the kernel's environment unless you pass `remember=True`. `forget_model()` deletes the saved copy.

## Limits [#limits]

* `exakit sql` connects with the admin profile. Anyone who can read your home folder as your user can read the admin password in `~/.exapump/config.toml`. So can root.
* The notebook connection store is encrypted, but its master password is a file in the same credentials folder. The store protects the connection details from a casual reader. It does not protect them from anyone who can read that folder.
* The kit has no scheduled password rotation. When `mcp-setup` runs, it reapplies the stored read-only password with `ALTER USER`. It generates a new one only when the stored value is missing or fails validation.
* The protection of the admin password is file permissions. No code in the kit calls the operating system's keychain.


# Security (/security)



This section is for a security reviewer, a platform engineer or a DBA. Every statement names the file and the function that does it, and quotes the behaviour from the code. Where the code does not do something, the page says so. Most pages end with a list of their limits.

The kit runs on your computer. It installs a local Exasol database, connects AI clients to it, and gives notebooks a way to ask questions. Its outbound calls are listed on the [Network and TLS](/security/network-and-tls) page.

## The trust boundaries [#the-trust-boundaries]

Two charts show where data and credentials move. The first is inside this computer.

<Flow
  caption="Inside this computer"
  steps="[
  { title: &#x22;You&#x22;, text: &#x22;Run exakit, answer its prompts, approve each SQL statement before a notebook runs it&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;The kit&#x22;, text: &#x22;The exakit scripts and the notebook helpers. They read the credentials folder when they run&#x22;, code: &#x22;exakit status&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Local database&#x22;, text: &#x22;The admin (SYS) user is used for setup and admin tasks&#x22;, tone: &#x22;db&#x22;, href: &#x22;/security/credentials&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Read-only MCP user&#x22;, text: &#x22;mcp_readonly. It can read, not write. The database rejects writes&#x22;, tone: &#x22;db&#x22;, href: &#x22;/security/ai-clients&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;AI client&#x22;, text: &#x22;Reads through the Exasol MCP server on 127.0.0.1&#x22;, tone: &#x22;ai&#x22;, href: &#x22;/security/ai-clients&#x22; },
]"
/>

The second is what leaves this computer, and when.

<Flow
  caption="What leaves this computer, and when"
  steps="[
  { title: &#x22;You start it&#x22;, text: &#x22;exakit marketplace, exakit update, or a model or source you chose&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Add-on downloads&#x22;, text: &#x22;From GitHub or S3 over HTTPS. The version and SHA-256 are pinned&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/security/add-ons-and-downloads&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;AI model provider&#x22;, text: &#x22;Only when you set one. Column names, types, roles and a few values. No rows&#x22;, tone: &#x22;ai&#x22;, href: &#x22;/security/what-goes-to-a-model&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;External source&#x22;, text: &#x22;Read live by the database through a virtual schema. TLS is verified by default&#x22;, tone: &#x22;db&#x22;, href: &#x22;/security/network-and-tls&#x22; },
]"
/>

    The database certificate pin, the addresses the kit listens on, the outbound calls it makes, and how external sources are verified.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Add-ons and downloads" href="/security/add-ons-and-downloads">
    Pinned versions and SHA-256 digests, the check before anything is unpacked, add-ons the kit did not install, and removal.
  </Card>

  <Card title="What the kit writes" href="/security/what-the-kit-writes">
    The schemas the kit creates, which of your tables it will change and when, and the files it keeps on this computer.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Report a security issue" href="/security/report-an-issue">
    Where to send a vulnerability, and what the repository does and does not publish about it.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## Known limits, from the code [#known-limits-from-the-code]

These are the places where the code does less than a reader might assume. Each is explained on its page.

| Limit                                        | What the code does                                                                                                                                                           | Where                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `exakit sql` runs as the admin user          | It uses the exapump admin profile and is not sandboxed. The read-only boundary is the MCP user, not this command                                                             | [AI clients](/security/ai-clients)                        |
| The read-only user reads every table         | It holds `SELECT ANY TABLE`, so an AI client can query personal-data columns. The sensitive-column rule limits what the kit sends to a model, not what the MCP user can read | [AI clients](/security/ai-clients)                        |
| The MCP server has no token                  | It runs with `--no-auth` on 127.0.0.1. Any program on this computer that reaches the port can send read queries                                                              | [AI clients](/security/ai-clients)                        |
| The MCP server connection is not pinned here | The sidecar definition sets `EXA_DSN` to the plain host and port and `EXA_SSL_CERT_VALIDATION` to `false`. The certificate pin is added to the other clients only            | [Network and TLS](/security/network-and-tls)              |
| One helper sends row text                    | `nb.themes()` sends the text of the rows you select to your model, up to 600 characters each. The sensitive-column rule does not apply to it                                 | [What is sent to a model](/security/what-goes-to-a-model) |
| Three add-ons can skip their checksum        | Setting `EXAKIT_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_EXASOL_VSCODE`, `EXAKIT_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_EXASOL_SCHEDULER` or `EXAKIT_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_JSON_TABLES` to `1` installs without a digest        | [Add-ons and downloads](/security/add-ons-and-downloads)  |
| A pasted connection string can lower TLS     | A SQL Server string with `encrypt=false` sets `tls=disable` for that source. You see the reading before you confirm it                                                       | [Network and TLS](/security/network-and-tls)              |
| Your passwords are plain text in a 0600 file | The admin password sits in the exapump profile, and the notebook store master password sits beside its store. Both are protected by file permissions only                    | [Credentials](/security/credentials)                      |


# Network and TLS (/security/network-and-tls)



The kit listens on this computer only. Its outbound calls are few and listed below. The one that needs the most care is the database connection, because the database uses a self-signed certificate that no client can check against a certificate authority.

## The database certificate is pinned [#the-database-certificate-is-pinned]

The kit records the database's certificate fingerprint once, then every client it builds checks that the port still serves that certificate.

* **What is recorded.** The SHA-256 of the server's DER certificate, as lowercase hex. `fingerprint()` in `setup/lib/tls_pin.py` computes it. It reads the certificate without validating it, because reading it is the point. The value is stored in the manifest as `runtime.tls_fingerprint`, with the time in `runtime.tls_fingerprint_at`.
* **When it is recorded.** When the kit deploys or starts its own database, `exakit_tls_record()` in `setup/lib/common.sh` records the certificate. This is trust on first use, as the code's comment calls it.
* **Who checks it.** The exapump profile gets `certificate_fingerprint` (`exapump_write_profile()` in `setup/lib/exapump.sh`). A pyexasol connection gets the DSN `host/<fingerprint>:port` (`exakit_tls_pinned_dsn()` in `setup/lib/common.sh`). The notebook's `connect()` pins the same way (`_pinned()` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/__init__.py`).
* **What a mismatch does.** A client refuses a certificate that does not match. `exakit tls-pin` compares the pinned and live values and changes nothing. `exakit tls-pin --accept` records the live certificate, after a question that defaults to no when a pin is being replaced. Its exit code is `6` when the live certificate is not the pinned one (`setup/help/exakit.json`).

The profiles also carry `validate_certificate = false`. That is deliberate: the certificate is self-signed, so the pin is the check. Without a recorded pin, nothing validates the certificate.

Exasol's own documentation describes the same approach for clients that cannot verify a certificate: a SHA-256 fingerprint, which changes whenever the certificate is replaced. See [Upload TLS certificate](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/administration/on-premise/access_management/tls_certificate.htm).

### Installs made before the pin existed [#installs-made-before-the-pin-existed]

`exakit_tls_ensure_pinned()` in `setup/lib/common.sh` records a pin the first time a kit command finds the database running and answering. The pin then trusts whatever answered on the port at that time. The code does not compare it with anything earlier.

### The MCP server connection is not pinned in this code [#the-mcp-server-connection-is-not-pinned-in-this-code]

`_mcp_sidecar_definition()` in `setup/lib/mcp.sh` sets the server's connection like this:

```text
EXA_DSN          = $(EXASOL_DB_HOST):$(EXASOL_DB_PORT)     no fingerprint
EXA_SSL_CERT_VALIDATION = "false"
```

`exakit_tls_rewrite_clients()` in `setup/lib/common.sh` says that "the launcher's sidecar entries hold no DSN". The pin reaches the stdio form of the server's `EXA_DSN`, and the other kit clients. It does not reach the sidecar definition in this repository. Whether the launcher adds a pin elsewhere is outside this repository, so this page does not claim one.

## Addresses the kit listens on [#addresses-the-kit-listens-on]

| Listener                      | Address                                             | Source                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Notebook documentation server | `127.0.0.1` (the page is shown as `localhost`)      | `BIND` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/docs.py`. Its comment says "no other computer reaches it" |
| Exasol MCP server             | `127.0.0.1:4896`, with `--no-auth`                  | `hostIP` and `args` in `_mcp_sidecar_definition()`, `setup/lib/mcp.sh`                          |
| Database                      | The port recorded in the manifest, on this computer | `runtime.dsn` in the manifest                                                                   |

The MCP server has no token. See [AI clients](/security/ai-clients).

## Every outbound call the kit makes [#every-outbound-call-the-kit-makes]

| Call                         | Destination                                                          | When                                                             | Source                                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Install and update downloads | GitHub release URLs and the launcher's S3 bucket, over HTTPS         | When you install, update or repair                               | `versions.json`; see [Add-ons and downloads](/security/add-ons-and-downloads) |
| Public IP lookup             | `https://checkip.amazonaws.com`, one request per run, 3-second limit | When a source command runs. Skipped with `EXAKIT_NO_IP_LOOKUP=1` | `setup/virtual-schemas/engine/publicip.py`                                    |
| Your model                   | The address in `EXAKIT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`                            | Only when you use a model helper                                 | [What is sent to a model](/security/what-goes-to-a-model)                     |
| Langfuse                     | The address in `LANGFUSE_BASE_URL`                                   | Only when tracing is on                                          | [What is sent to a model](/security/what-goes-to-a-model)                     |
| External sources             | The source you connected                                             | When the database reads it                                       | [External sources](#external-sources) below                                   |

The public IP is one address and a newline. The module says it is "advice, never a step". It is for allow-listing this computer at a source that filters by address. If the lookup fails, the address is reported as unknown.

Telemetry is turned off by default. `marketplace/kit_telemetry.py` sets `EXASOL_TELEMETRY_DISABLE`, `DBT_SEND_ANONYMOUS_USAGE_STATS=false` and `MLFLOW_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true` for every process the kit starts, unless you set those variables yourself.

## External sources [#external-sources]

A source is read where it lives. The database connects to it through a virtual schema, and the connection's TLS setting decides how the certificate is checked.

* **The default is `verify`.** `setup/virtual-schemas/engine/paste.py` says "tls stays at verify (TCPS, the kit's default)". The engine's failure advice in `setup/virtual-schemas/engine/lifecycle.py`, `tls_fix()`, names the fix: "fix the server certificate", or give the CA that signs it with `--set ca=<PEM file or bundle>`.
* **`require` encrypts without checking.** `tls_fix()` says it is used "only knowingly". The engine's own advice in `setup/virtual-schemas/engine/sql.py` calls it "encrypts without checking the certificate".
* **A pasted string can change the setting.** `tls_sqlserver()` in `setup/virtual-schemas/engine/paste.py` maps `encrypt=false` to `disable`, and `TrustServerCertificate=true` to `require`. Those values come from the string you paste, not from the kit's defaults. Before you confirm the connection, the kit shows the reading back with its secrets masked. The shell prints it as `Read: ...` in `_exakit_vs_tui_paste()` in `setup/lib/virtual-schemas.sh`.
* **The kit does not lower the setting by itself.** When the paste does not say otherwise, the engine keeps `verify`. An unknown `encrypt` value is reported, and `tls` stays at its default.

## Limits [#limits]

* The pin is recorded on first use. It trusts whatever answered on the port at that moment.
* The MCP server's connection to the database is not pinned in this repository.
* The database connection uses `validate_certificate = false` alongside the pin.
* A pasted SQL Server string can set `tls=disable` for a source. The kit shows that reading before you confirm, but the choice is yours.
* Telemetry is off only for the processes the kit starts. Tools you run yourself follow their own settings.


# Report a security issue (/security/report-an-issue)



Send a suspected vulnerability to **[plg.connect@exasol.com](mailto:plg.connect@exasol.com)**. That is the address the documentation's Feedback button uses (`FEEDBACK_ADDRESS` in `notebook/docs/components/feedback.tsx`), and the one the repository's issue chooser offers as "Write to the team" (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`).

## What the repository does not publish [#what-the-repository-does-not-publish]

* There is no `SECURITY.md` file in the repository root. This page does not link one, and it does not invent a disclosure process, a response time or a security contact other than the address above.
* The repository does not state how the team handles a report after it arrives. Nothing in this section describes that process.

## What to include [#what-to-include]

Describe what you did and what you saw. These help the team reproduce it:

* The kit version, from `exakit status --json`.
* The command or notebook cell, and the file or page it came from.
* Your operating system and whether you ran the Windows or the Unix installer.
* What you expected, and what happened instead.

Read the output before you send it. The kit redacts the secrets listed on the [Credentials](/security/credentials) page in the places that page names. Logs can still hold your data, file paths and table names.

## What not to send [#what-not-to-send]

Do not send the contents of `~/.exasol-starter-kit/credentials/`, `~/.exapump/config.toml`, the notebook connection store, or an `exakit.env` file. Describe the problem without them.

## A problem that is not a vulnerability [#a-problem-that-is-not-a-vulnerability]

For an ordinary problem with the kit, the repository's issue chooser suggests an issue with the output of `exakit status --json` and `exakit logs`. Check that output for anything private before you post it in public.

<Callout>
  `exakit tls-pin` with no options compares the pinned certificate with the live one and changes nothing. `exakit mcp-doctor` tests the AI connection and repairs it, so run it only when you are ready for a repair.
</Callout>


# What is sent to an AI model (/security/what-goes-to-a-model)



The kit calls a model only when you set one. Set `EXAKIT_MODEL_ID` and `EXAKIT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, and the helpers below call that address. The request is Chat Completions. Every model client is built by `create_client()` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/model_config.py`. The model is your choice, and the kit does not check the provider's data-retention terms.

## Which helper sends what [#which-helper-sends-what]

| Helper                       | Where it is                                                                                                     | What the model receives                                                                                                                                                                                                       | What it never receives                           |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `ask()`                      | `notebook/package/exakit_nb/ask.py`, `described()`                                                              | The table name, the descriptor version, the slots, and each column's role, evidence and note. The question. A sensitive column appears by name and role only, with the instruction "never select, group or filter its values" | Rows. Values of sensitive columns                |
| Model notes                  | `setup/lib/describe_service.py`, `model_notes()`                                                                | For each non-sensitive column: its name, type, role, evidence and up to five of its most frequent values                                                                                                                      | Sensitive columns, which are skipped entirely    |
| Semantic Views drafting      | `setup/lib/describe_service.py`, `semantic_ai()`, with `ai_facts()` in `setup/lib/descriptor/semantic_model.py` | Entity names and tables, grains, relationships, dimension and fact names and comments, metric expressions, and up to ten values of a category dimension                                                                       | Private facts. Sensitive columns carry no values |
| Feature ideas with `ai=True` | `notebook/package/exakit_nb/lab.py`, `feature_ideas()`                                                          | Non-sensitive column names and roles, the target name, and model scores                                                                                                                                                       | Row values                                       |
| `nb.themes()`                | `notebook/package/exakit_nb/themes.py`                                                                          | The text of the rows in the sample you pass in, up to 600 characters each, one call per side of the label                                                                                                                     | Nothing is filtered. See the warning below       |

<Callout type="warn">
  `nb.themes()` sends row text to your model. It is the only helper that sends the content of rows. The kit does not check whether that text column is sensitive. The SQL in the notebook cell chooses the rows, so the sensitive-column rule does not apply to them.
</Callout>

### A flag column gives its values [#a-flag-column-gives-its-values]

A flag is a column with two values. For a flag, the evidence in the descriptor holds both values, and the evidence is sent to the model. `ask()`'s rules say so: "A flag's evidence gives its values." So a non-sensitive flag such as `CANCELLED` reaches the model with its two values, as do the values of a category.

## How sensitive columns are found [#how-sensitive-columns-are-found]

`setup/lib/descriptor/roles.py` decides sensitivity before the role, and keeps it whatever the role is. Its docstring gives the rules. A text column is sensitive when:

* 90% or more of its values are e-mail addresses, phone numbers, IBANs or 5-digit postcodes, or
* its name says postcode (ZIP, POSTAL, PLZ) and 90% of its values are shaped like one, or
* its name says a person's name (`FIRST_NAME`, `SURNAME`, `CUSTOMER_NAME`, `DRIVER_NAME`), or
* it is an address whose values are long and mostly distinct (`STREET_ADDRESS`, though not `ADDR_STATE`).

A sensitive column gets the role `identifier`. `_finish()` in `setup/lib/descriptor/profile.py` keeps counts for it and drops its top values, minimum and maximum. The module docstring of `setup/lib/descriptor/store.py` says the profile file holds "no value of a sensitive column, because these files end up in bug reports."

<Callout>
  Detection is a set of patterns. It can miss personal data that does not match them, for example a free-text note that contains a name. Check a column map before you approve it, and mark a column yourself if it is wrong.
</Callout>

## Where a key may travel [#where-a-key-may-travel]

`resolve()` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/model_config.py` refuses to build a client with a key unless the address passes `clear_text_ok()`:

* `https://` to any host, or
* `http://` only to `localhost`, a `.local` or `.internal` name, or a loopback, private or link-local address.

Anything else raises `... would send EXAKIT_PROVIDER_API_KEY in clear text`, before a request is made. `setup_env.use_model()` applies the same test before it asks for a key, and prints a note instead.

Two gaps follow from the code, and they are stated here so they are not assumed away:

* With no key set, `resolve()` accepts a plain `http://` address to any host. No key is sent, but the prompts and answers travel in clear text.
* The `clear_text_ok()` test applies to the Langfuse address only inside `use_model()`. A Langfuse address set in your shell or in `exakit.env` is not checked.

## Tracing is opt-in [#tracing-is-opt-in]

`tracing()` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/__init__.py` returns true only when `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_BASE_URL` (or `LANGFUSE_HOST`) are all set. Without them, `create_client()` builds a plain OpenAI client, and nothing is sent to Langfuse. With them, `model_client()` returns Langfuse's wrapper for the same OpenAI call, and each call is recorded in your Langfuse project. The kit adds no filter to what the wrapper records beyond the rules in the table above.

## Limits [#limits]

* The kit sends what the table above lists. Your model provider handles that data under its own terms.
* A model that sees column names and values can infer what a sensitive column holds. The kit keeps the values out, not the inference.
* Plain `http://` to a public host, with no key, is not blocked.
* The Langfuse address rule is not applied outside `use_model()`.
* `nb.themes()` sends the text of the rows you choose.


# What the kit writes (/security/what-the-kit-writes)



The kit writes to two places: your database and your computer. This page lists what it creates, what it changes, and what it will not touch.

## Schemas in the database [#schemas-in-the-database]

| Schema or object                                        | What it holds                                                                                                                                                        | Created by                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `STARTER_KIT`                                           | The default schema of the read-only user, where local uploads land. Created if it is missing                                                                         | `exakit_configure_mcp_readonly_access()`, `setup/lib/common.sh`                                                                                                          |
| The sample dataset schemas, such as `AMAZON` and `TPCH` | The bundled sample data. Created by each dataset's own `01_create_schema.sql` in `data/datasets/<name>/`                                                             | `exakit data-load <name>`                                                                                                                                                |
| `EXAKIT_PREPARED`                                       | Joined views and typed, cleaned views you choose to create                                                                                                           | `SCHEMA = "EXAKIT_PREPARED"` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/prepare.py`, and `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS EXAKIT_PREPARED` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/schema_map.py` |
| `SEMANTIC_CATALOG`, `SEMANTIC_ADMIN`, `SEMANTIC_AGENT`  | Exasol Semantic Views' own schemas. `SEMANTIC_CATALOG` holds the models' metadata, which any read-only client can read, for example `SEMANTIC_CATALOG.RELATIONSHIPS` | `setup/lib/descriptor/schema.py` and `setup/lib/descriptor/publish.py`                                                                                                   |
| `SEM_<MODEL>`                                           | A published semantic model's views                                                                                                                                   | `setup/lib/descriptor/publish.py`                                                                                                                                        |
| `VS_<NAME>`, and a CONNECTION named `EXAKIT_SRC_<NAME>` | An external source's virtual schema, and its connection                                                                                                              | `setup/virtual-schemas/engine/plan.py`, where `"connection": "EXAKIT_SRC_%s"` and `"schema": "VS_%s"` are set                                                            |

## Your tables [#your-tables]

The kit changes a table you own only when you tell it to. Three paths can do so.

**Loading a file (`exakit data-load`, `nb.load_own_file()`).** The kit does not overwrite a table it did not load. `load_own_file()` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/own_file.py` stops with "already exists and was not loaded by load_own_file" unless you pass `replace=True`. For `exakit data-load`, `EXAKIT_ON_EXISTING` decides:

* `skip`, the default. A table with rows the kit did not load is left alone. The command exits with code 5 and changes nothing (`setup/lib/exapump.sh`).
* `replace`. The table is dropped and rebuilt from the file. The code comment says "DROP, not TRUNCATE". The load receipt is removed with it.
* `append`. The file's rows are added on top of the existing rows.

**Writing SQL from the terminal (`exakit sql --write`).** This runs as the admin, so it can change any table. See [AI clients](/security/ai-clients).

**Approving a column map.** Approval writes a descriptor under `~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/`. It changes the database only through Semantic Views, in the schemas listed above.

### Comments the kit adds [#comments-the-kit-adds]

When the kit loads a file, it marks the table with `COMMENT ON TABLE`. The mark holds the file's SHA-256, and it is written only on a table the kit has just created or replaced. That mark is how the kit recognises a table it loaded, so a later load can skip it. Outside that load, the kit issues no `ALTER TABLE` and no other `COMMENT ON`. A search of `setup/` and `notebook/package/exakit_nb/` confirms this. The `replace` and `append` paths above are the exception, because you chose them.

`setup/lib/descriptor/schema.py` states the same rule for schema maps: "the user's own schema and tables are never commented or altered."

## Files on this computer [#files-on-this-computer]

Everything is under the kit home, `~/.exasol-starter-kit` (or `EXAKIT_HOME`). Three rules apply to the files there:

* **Secrets** are in `credentials/`. See [Credentials](/security/credentials).
* **Logs and records** are written at mode 600 on Unix. The workflow log is opened with `os.open(..., 0o600)` in `notebook/package/exakit_nb/workflow.py`. The virtual schema log is "created owner-only (mode 600)" according to `setup/virtual-schemas/engine/vslog.py`.
* **Hand-off bundles** get mode 700 for folders and 600 for files, set by `handoff_bundle.py`. Those modes are not applied on Windows, which the code checks with `os.name != "nt"`.

### The approved column maps [#the-approved-column-maps]

Each approved column map is kept as a version, in `~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<SCHEMA>.<TABLE>/`. The module docstring of `setup/lib/descriptor/store.py` gives the layout:

* `v<n>.yaml` is written exclusively. "A version file is created exclusively, so v(n) is never touched." An approval never rewrites an earlier version.
* `current.yaml` is replaced through a temporary file and `os.replace`.
* `draft.yaml` and `profile.json` hold the work in progress. The profile has no value of a sensitive column.

A whole schema's map (its tables and the links between them) is kept the same way, in `descriptors/<SCHEMA>/`, with `v<n>.json` files. `setup/lib/descriptor/schema.py` says those are never rewritten.

### The shell profile [#the-shell-profile]

The installer adds the kit's `bin` folder to your shell profile, through `ensure_path_hint()` in `setup/lib/common.sh`. If `EXAKIT_NO_PROFILE_EDIT=1` is set, it prints the line for you to add instead. The full uninstall leaves that line in place, as the comment above `exakit_uninstall_run()` in `setup/lib/common.sh` says. Remove the line yourself if you want it gone.

## What the kit leaves alone [#what-the-kit-leaves-alone]

* A table holding rows the kit did not load, unless you choose `replace` or `append`.
* A notebook you edited. The [Notebooks](/kit/tools/notebooks) page says an edited notebook is never overwritten.
* Approved column maps, workflow logs and bundles. The [Where things live](/data-scientist/development/where-things-live) page says an update leaves them alone.
* An add-on installation the kit did not make. See [Add-ons and downloads](/security/add-ons-and-downloads).

## Limits [#limits]

* `exakit data-load` with `replace` drops a table you own. On a terminal you are asked which policy applies. Without a terminal the policy is `skip`, unless `EXAKIT_ON_EXISTING` says otherwise.
* `exakit sql --write` can change any table, as the admin.
* On Windows, the Unix modes above are not applied. The NTFS permissions described in [Credentials](/security/credentials) are the protection there.
* The virtual schema log removes its files older than `KEEP_DAYS` when a new day's file is opened (`setup/virtual-schemas/engine/vslog.py`). This page found no pruning rule for the other logs.


# The data science workflow (/data-scientist)



Most data science work is not a straight line. You set up, load the data, look at it, prepare it, model it and check the result. Then a finding in a later stage sends you back. A column you trusted turns out to give away the answer, so you prepare the data again. Treat the eight stages as a loop, not a checklist.

Choose a stage to read its page. Each page says what the stage is for, where you do it in the kit, a worked example on the kit's sample data, and what can go wrong.

<StageMap />

## How the kit fits in [#how-the-kit-fits-in]

The kit runs this workflow on an Exasol database on your computer. Four notebooks take you through the stages in order. Each notebook continues the same workflow, so you paste no id and copy nothing between them.

<Flow
  caption="The four notebooks, in order, and the stages each one covers"
  steps="[
  { title: &#x22;00_quickstart&#x22;, text: &#x22;Set up Exasol, Get the data, and the column map of Explore and understand&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/set-up&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;01_explore&#x22;, text: &#x22;Prepare, Explore, Model and Evaluate&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/prepare&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;02_ask_your_data&#x22;, text: &#x22;Explore and understand: asking questions in plain language&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/explore&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;03_share&#x22;, text: &#x22;Communicate and deploy: a dashboard and a hand-off folder&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/communicate&#x22; },
]"
/>

Monitor and iterate has no notebook of its own. The workflow log records what you did, and you iterate by changing the column map or the data and running the notebooks again. The notebooks read the newest approval.

## Two ways through each notebook [#two-ways-through-each-notebook]

Every notebook opens with a **guided card**. A card has buttons and forms for the page's steps. Each card has a **Guided / Code** switch at its top right.

* **Guided** is the default. You click, choose and approve.
* **Code** turns the same card into its code as cells. Each cell shows the exact `exakit.nb` call behind a control. You can edit and run those cells.

Every button is one call, so clicking **Approve** and running the approve call do the same thing. The notebook's own code sits below the cards. You can use either way, or switch between them as you work.

## Developers [#developers]

If you build on the kit, or want the commands behind the notebooks, see [For developers](/data-scientist/development). It has the command reference, how the cards and helpers fit together, and where the kit keeps its files.


# Column maps (/kit/data/column-maps)



A **column map** (the descriptor) gives every column of a table a role. Notebooks and AI clients read it, so they all work from the same meaning. For the idea behind it, see [Column map and approval](/data-scientist/explore).

## Draft [#draft]

```bash
exakit describe AMAZON.ORDER_LINES
```

The table is profiled with SELECTs only. Nothing is written to the database. Every column gets one of eight roles, with its confidence and the evidence that chose it:

`key`, `time`, `measure`, `category`, `flag`, `text`, `identifier`, `other`.

* The draft is deterministic: the same table gives the same draft.
* A column whose values look like e-mail addresses, phone numbers, IBANs or postcodes is marked **sensitive**.
* The **target** is never drafted. Only a person sets it.

## Approve [#approve]

```bash
exakit describe AMAZON.ORDER_LINES --approve --role target=CANCELLED --owner dana
```

`--role <slot>=<COLUMN>` corrects a slot: `key`, `time`, `text`, `target`, `category`, `entity`. `<slot>=-` leaves it empty.

Approval:

* checks that every column has a role, that none sits in two slots, and that the table has not changed since it was profiled
* writes a new version, never rewriting an old one
* publishes the roles in [Exasol Semantic Views](/kit/data/semantic-views): the schema's semantic model is rebuilt with this table as an entity, readable by the read-only AI user. Semantic Views is installed first when the database does not have it yet.

Your own table is never commented. If publishing fails, the approval still stands and the message says why.

## What you get at the end [#what-you-get-at-the-end]

A new version of the column map, kept under `~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/`, and the schema's semantic model (its views in `SEM_<SCHEMA>`) rebuilt from it. The notebooks and AI clients read the approved version from then on.

## See and compare [#see-and-compare]

```bash
exakit describe amazon_sales --show              # the current version
exakit describe amazon_sales --show --version 1  # an earlier one
exakit describe amazon_sales --versions          # every version
exakit describe orders --comments                # rebuild the schema's semantic model again
```

Add `--json` to any of them for a script.

## A whole schema [#a-whole-schema]

```bash
exakit describe --schema TPCH
```

This lists every table with its rows and key, and every many-to-one link between tables with its evidence. A link is a foreign key the database declares, or a column whose values are in another table's key (at most 0.1% of them may be missing). A name alone never makes a link.

```bash
exakit describe --schema TPCH --approve --unlink ORDERS.O_CLERK
```

`--link TABLE.COLUMN=TABLE.KEY` adds a link and `--unlink TABLE.COLUMN` removes one. The approved links become relationships of the schema's semantic model. To join tables of different schemas, build a [multi-source model](/kit/data/semantic-views).

## Where they are kept [#where-they-are-kept]

`~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<SCHEMA>.<TABLE>/`: the draft, every approved version and the current one.

## When the table changes [#when-the-table-changes]

Columns whose name and type did not change keep their approved roles. The rest are flagged, and you approve again.

## With an AI model [#with-an-ai-model]

When a model is set up, one call adds a one-line note per column. It is sent each column's name, type, role, evidence and top values, never a row and never a sensitive column. A note never decides a role.

## From a notebook [#from-a-notebook]

```python
draft = nb.describe("AMAZON.ORDER_LINES")
draft.slot(target="CANCELLED")
dataset = draft.approve()
```

See [Review and approve the column map](/data-scientist/explore).


# Datasets (/kit/data/datasets)



The kit carries sample datasets to practise on. `exakit data-load` lists them and loads the ones you pick.

| Dataset              | Loaded by                   | Where it comes from                          |
| -------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `tpch`               | General                     | Bundled with the kit, loads without internet |
| `energy`             | General                     | Bundled with the kit, loads without internet |
| `weather`            | General                     | Bundled with the kit, loads without internet |
| `amazon_sales`       | Data Scientist, ML Engineer | Downloaded when you load it                  |
| `fraud_transactions` | Data Scientist, ML Engineer | Downloaded when you load it                  |

## Downloaded datasets [#downloaded-datasets]

`amazon_sales` and `fraud_transactions` are archives in the kit's datasets release. An archive is fetched only when you load that dataset. The kit checks the archive's SHA-256 and every file's digest, and refuses a mismatch.

```bash
exakit data-load amazon_sales
```

## A dataset with a column map [#a-dataset-with-a-column-map]

`amazon_sales` and `fraud_transactions` each ship with an approved [column map](/kit/data/column-maps), so the notebooks can use them straight away. You can approve your own version at any time.

The ML Engineer persona is not offered in this release, so for now only Data Scientist and General load these datasets.

## Load one again [#load-one-again]

```bash
exakit data-load --force amazon_sales
```

<Callout type="warn">
  `--force` drops that dataset's tables and rebuilds them. Anything you changed in its schema is lost.
</Callout>

## Add a dataset to the kit [#add-a-dataset-to-the-kit]

A dataset is one folder in `data/datasets/`. Nothing else names it, so a new folder appears in the menu.


# Load data (/kit/data/load-data)



```bash
exakit data-load
```

On a terminal this opens a menu: the kit's datasets, your own data, or an external source. Name what you want to skip the menu.

<Tabs items="['A kit dataset', 'One file', 'A folder']">
  <Tab value="A kit dataset">
    ```bash
    exakit data-load amazon_sales
    ```

    See [Datasets](/kit/data/datasets) for the list.
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="One file">
    ```bash
    exakit data-load ./sales.csv
    ```

    It asks two things, whatever the file's kind: the file, then `SCHEMA.TABLE`. To answer up front:

    ```bash
    EXAKIT_DATA_FILE=./sales.json EXAKIT_DATA_TABLE=STARTER_KIT.SALES exakit data-load
    ```

    CSV, Parquet and JSON are loaded. JSON is split into tables by an engine the kit installs for you on macOS, Linux and WSL. A `;`-separated CSV is loaded with its delimiter. A tabular `.txt` or `.tsv` file is listed with the rename to `.csv` that the loader needs.
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="A folder">
    ```bash
    exakit data-load ~/exports
    ```

    Every CSV, Parquet and JSON (.json, .geojson) file at the folder's top level becomes one table named after the file. The schema is asked once:

    ```bash
    EXAKIT_DATA_FILE=~/exports EXAKIT_SCHEMA=SALES exakit data-load
    ```

    Subfolders are not scanned. Files of other kinds are ignored. Duplicates are skipped with the reason. On Windows, a folder's JSON files are listed as skipped.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Running it again is safe [#running-it-again-is-safe]

* A file already loaded is skipped, not loaded on top of itself.
* A file that a stopped run left half-written is loaded again from scratch.
* A table holding rows this kit did not load is left alone, unless you say otherwise.

```bash
EXAKIT_ON_EXISTING=replace exakit data-load ~/exports
```

`EXAKIT_ON_EXISTING` takes `skip` (the default), `replace` or `append`. Without a terminal the answer is `skip`. On a terminal you are asked.

## What you get at the end [#what-you-get-at-the-end]

Every file is listed with its table and the rows that landed, or the reason it did not load. A file the loader refuses leaves no empty table behind.

## From a notebook [#from-a-notebook]

```python
nb.exakit("data-load", "fraud_transactions")
own_data = nb.load_own_file("~/sales-data/orders.csv", "SALES", conn=connection)
```

See [Load data in the Data Scientist notebooks](/data-scientist/get-the-data).

## An external source [#an-external-source]

Data in another database is not copied. It is connected with `exakit connect` and read where it lives. See [Sources](/data-scientist/get-the-data).

## Further reading [#further-reading]

* [IMPORT](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/sql/import.htm), the statement that moves data into a table.
* [Load data from local or remote files](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/loading_data/load_data_local_remote_location.htm) and [Load data from external sources](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/loading_data/load_data_from_externalsources.htm).
* [Virtual Schemas](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/virtual_schemas.htm) and the [Virtual Schema User Guide](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/virtual_schema/user_guide.htm), for the external sources the kit connects.
* [exapump](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exapump), the command-line client the kit uses to load files.
* [exasol/virtual-schemas](https://github.com/exasol/virtual-schemas), the entry-point repository for Exasol's virtual schemas.
* [How the kit handles credentials and external sources](/security/credentials).


# Run SQL (/kit/data/run-sql)



```bash
exakit sql 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM AMAZON.ORDER_LINES'
```

It runs one statement and prints the result.

## Reads only unless you say otherwise [#reads-only-unless-you-say-otherwise]

A statement that would change data is refused unless you add `--write`.

```bash
exakit sql --write 'CREATE SCHEMA SCRATCH'
```

<Callout type="warn">
  `exakit sql` connects as the kit's admin user, and that user is not sandboxed. The read-only boundary is the MCP user that AI clients use, not this command.
</Callout>

## A saved statement [#a-saved-statement]

```bash
exakit sql --file ./report.sql
```

Comment lines and a trailing semicolon are dropped first. A statement can also come on standard input.

## Errors come with their fix [#errors-come-with-their-fix]

The three faults everyone hits first are turned into what to do:

| Fault                  | What you are told  |
| ---------------------- | ------------------ |
| Connection refused     | Run `exakit start` |
| `FETCH FIRST` or `TOP` | Use `LIMIT`        |
| Object not found       | Describe it first  |

The fix is printed first, with the error.

## For a script [#for-a-script]

```bash
exakit sql --json 'SELECT 1'
```

One JSON object comes back and nothing else: the rows and their count on success, or the error with a command to run, when there is one.

<Callout>
  On Windows PowerShell 5.1, a double quote inside an argument is dropped before `exakit` runs. Pass a statement with quoted names through `--file`.
</Callout>

## Further reading [#further-reading]

* [SELECT](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/sql/select.htm), the statement the examples on this page use.
* [Privileges](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/privileges.htm), the rules behind the admin and read-only users.
* [exapump](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exapump), the command-line client the kit uses for SQL and loading.
* [AI clients and the read-only user](/security/ai-clients), which explains why `exakit sql` is not the read-only path.


# Semantic fusion (/kit/data/semantic-fusion)



Your data lives in more than one place: a database here, files there, a cloud source somewhere else. The usual answer is to copy everything into one store first (ETL). The kit does not. It reads each source where it is, agrees once on what the data means, and answers from that. Only answers travel back.

<Flow
  caption="Sources stay where they are. One model gives them one meaning."
  steps="[
  { title: &#x22;Sources&#x22;, text: &#x22;A PostgreSQL database, your files, sample data. Nothing is copied&#x22;, tone: &#x22;db&#x22;, href: &#x22;/kit/data/load-data&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Connect&#x22;, text: &#x22;An external source becomes a virtual schema, read live&#x22;, code: &#x22;exakit connect postgresql&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Agree on meaning&#x22;, text: &#x22;You approve what each column is&#x22;, code: &#x22;exakit describe ... --approve&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22;, href: &#x22;/kit/data/column-maps&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Fuse&#x22;, text: &#x22;Links found from the values, one semantic model over all of it&#x22;, code: &#x22;exakit describe --model ... --find-links&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/kit/data/semantic-views&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Use&#x22;, text: &#x22;Notebooks, AI clients and dashboards ask the same model&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22; },
]"
/>

## The four layers [#the-four-layers]

| Layer          | What it does                                                                             | Where the data is         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Connectors     | A virtual schema (`VS_<NAME>`) per external source. A query is pushed down to the source | Stays in the source       |
| Column maps    | Each column gets a role: key, time, measure, category. You approve it                    | Nothing moves             |
| Semantic model | Tables become entities, links become relationships, measures become metrics              | Definitions only, no rows |
| Answers        | Semantic SQL is compiled into one query over the live sources                            | Only the result returns   |

## An example, measured [#an-example-measured]

Three sources that share no key and no column names: Amazon order lines (sample data, 128,975 rows), a PostgreSQL logistics database read live, and a state population table.

**1. Find how they join.** No foreign key exists. The kit compares values:

```bash
exakit describe --links AMAZON,VS_LOGISTICS,RETAIL_SIGNALS
```

```text
[high] AMAZON.ORDER_LINES.SHIP_STATE -> VS_LOGISTICS.STATE_LOGISTICS.SHIP_STATE:
       128,921 of 128,942 rows match; 21 do not (ORISSA, RAJSHTHAN, ...)
```

The 21 rows are misspelt state names. The link stands, and you get the list to clean. It took 26 small queries.

**2. Put one model over them.**

```bash
exakit describe --model sales_360 --schemas AMAZON,RETAIL_SIGNALS --find-links
```

This published one model over the order lines and the state table, joined on the state name, a link found the same way. Why the link is there is stored with it. (The run was measured under a test model name; `sales_360` stands for it here. The PostgreSQL source was not reachable when the model was published, so its link from step 1 is not in these figures.)

**3. Ask it.** Revenue by region needs both sources. In Semantic SQL you name what you want, not how to join:

```sql
SELECT region, order_lines_count, total_amount
FROM SEM_SALES_360.ORDER_LINES GROUP BY region
```

| Region | Order lines | Revenue       |
| ------ | ----------- | ------------- |
| South  | 52,761      | 31,314,207.29 |
| North  | 30,148      | 19,245,528.38 |
| West   | 27,956      | 16,744,010.73 |

The model compiled that into one scan, one join and one `GROUP BY`. A hand-written join returned the same figures for all 128,975 rows.

## Who uses the model [#who-uses-the-model]

<Flow
  caption="One model, three ways to ask it"
  steps="[
  { title: &#x22;A notebook&#x22;, text: &#x22;Ask in plain language. The AI writes Semantic SQL, you approve the SQL&#x22;, code: &#x22;nb.ask(dataset, question, conn=connection)&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/explore/questions&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;An AI client&#x22;, text: &#x22;Claude Code, Codex, Cursor read the model over a read-only connection&#x22;, tone: &#x22;ai&#x22;, href: &#x22;/kit/tools/ai-clients-and-skills&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;A dashboard&#x22;, text: &#x22;A checked result becomes a live page on Dash Server&#x22;, code: &#x22;03_share&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/communicate&#x22; },
]"
/>
