All three read the same definitions, so *revenue* is the same number everywhere.

## What it costs [#what-it-costs]

| Measured                                        | Result                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Model query on 10,002,745 rows joined to 30,000 | 0.12 to 0.27 s (hand-written: 0.13 to 0.21 s) |
| Finding links across six schemas, 25 tables     | 223 small queries, about 60 s                 |
| Rows copied out of a source                     | 0                                             |

A live source answers at its own speed. Each query to it is a filter or an aggregate the source runs itself.

## The same pattern, larger [#the-same-pattern-larger]

The hospital chain reference build uses this pattern on three systems that share no patient id: a legacy system on PostgreSQL, a health record on MongoDB and an imaging archive on Amazon S3. Exasol reads all three in place, resolves 1,609 patient records to 1,223 people, and answers a question across them in 0.3 to 4 seconds. The images never pass through the database.

## Limits [#limits]

* A link between two plain number columns cannot be proven from the data: numbers in a sequence match by chance. The kit marks it for you to confirm.
* A table needs an approved column map before it joins a model.
* A source that is down cannot be asked. Nothing is cached unless you load a copy yourself.

## Further reading [#further-reading]

* [Semantic views](/kit/data/semantic-views): the commands
* [Links across sources](/data-scientist/explore/semantic-views#links-across-sources): how links are found and what was measured
* [Virtual schemas](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/virtual_schemas.htm) in the Exasol documentation
* [Exasol Semantic Views](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-semantic-views) on GitHub


# Semantic views (/kit/data/semantic-views)



The kit's semantic layer is **Exasol Semantic Views**, the database's own semantic layer. A model says what your data means in business terms: its entities (tables), the relationships between them, the dimensions you group by and the metrics you ask for. AI clients read it over MCP and answer from its metrics; notebooks ask it with Semantic SQL.

You do not write a model by hand. The kit builds it from what you approved:

| You approved                          | It becomes                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A table's column map                  | An entity, with its key and grain                               |
| A link between two tables             | A relationship (many-to-one)                                    |
| A `time`, `category` or `flag` column | A dimension (a time column also gives `<column>_month`)         |
| A `measure` column                    | A fact, and the metrics `total_<column>` and `average_<column>` |
| Every table                           | A row count, `<table>_count`                                    |

A column marked **sensitive** is never a dimension and never a public fact.

## Installed when it is needed [#installed-when-it-is-needed]

Semantic Views is a marketplace add-on (`semantic-views`). The first approval installs it into the database, as this would:

```bash
exakit marketplace semantic-views
```

If that install fails, the approval still stands and says which command to run.

## One model per schema [#one-model-per-schema]

Approving a column map rebuilds its schema's model:

```bash
exakit describe AMAZON.ORDER_LINES --approve --role target=CANCELLED
```

The model is named after the schema (`amazon`) and its views are published in `SEM_<SCHEMA>` (`SEM_AMAZON.ORDER_LINES`). Approving a schema's links (`exakit describe --schema AMAZON --approve`) rebuilds it with the links as relationships.

## One model across sources [#one-model-across-sources]

A question often needs more than one schema: a sample dataset, your own files and one or more external sources. Build one model over all of them:

```bash
exakit describe --model sales_360 \
  --table AMAZON.ORDER_LINES --table MY_DATA.TARGETS --table VS_LOGISTICS.COURIER_DAILY \
  --link AMAZON.ORDER_LINES.SHIP_STATE=VS_LOGISTICS.STATE_LOGISTICS.STATE \
  --ai --dry-run
```

* Every table needs an approved column map first.
* `--link SCHEMA.TABLE.COLUMN=SCHEMA.TABLE.KEY` joins tables of different schemas. The key side must be unique. The approved links of each schema are used too.
* An external source (a virtual schema, `VS_<NAME>`) is read live: nothing is copied.
* `--dry-run` prints what would be built and writes nothing. Run it again without `--dry-run` to publish.

### Whole schemas, and links found for you [#whole-schemas-and-links-found-for-you]

Name schemas and the kit takes every table of them that has an approved column map. `--find-links` looks for the joins between the schemas in the values, with no foreign key and no matching names needed:

```bash
exakit describe --links AMAZON,MY_DATA,VS_LOGISTICS                 # the links alone, each with its evidence
exakit describe --model all_data --schemas AMAZON,MY_DATA,VS_LOGISTICS --find-links --ai --dry-run
```

A text link the data backs is used. A link between plain numbers is only named, because numbers in a sequence match by chance: pass it with `--link` if it is right. A pair you or an AI client believes in is checked with `exakit describe --links A,B --link S.T.COL=S.T.KEY`. How the search works, and what it measured, is on [Semantic views](/data-scientist/explore/semantic-views#links-across-sources).

### Let the AI propose the fields [#let-the-ai-propose-the-fields]

With `--ai`, the model you set up for the kit (`EXAKIT_MODEL_ID` and `EXAKIT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`) proposes business names, comments and synonyms for every field, and the metrics people will ask for: filtered totals (completed revenue), differences and ratios.

It is sent names, types, grains, column notes and a category's most frequent values. It is never sent a row, and never a sensitive column.

Every proposed metric is checked before it is used: it may only add up a fact of its view, combine that view's metrics, and filter on a dimension with one of its known values. The product validates it again when it is applied. A refused one is skipped, and the output names it and says why.

## Keep it current [#keep-it-current]

A model is built from what was approved at the time.

* Approving a column map rebuilds its schema's model and every multi-source model the table is in.
* After a new link or a new table, rebuild a model yourself:

```bash
exakit describe --model sales_360 --refresh
exakit describe --models                         # every model, and which the kit can refresh
```

The kit only rebuilds models it built. A model of the same name that someone else made is left alone.

## Ask a model [#ask-a-model]

A published view is queried with Semantic SQL: its metrics, grouped by its dimensions.

```sql
EXECUTE SCRIPT SEMANTIC_ADMIN.ENABLE_SEMANTIC_SQL();
SELECT ship_state, total_amount, orders_count
FROM SEM_SALES_360.ORDER_LINES
GROUP BY ship_state;
```

An AI client sets the preprocessor through the Exasol MCP server (`set_exasol_preprocessor`) and runs the same query. To see what a model holds, read `SEMANTIC_CATALOG.MODELS`, `ENTITIES`, `DIMENSIONS`, `METRICS` and `RELATIONSHIPS`.

## From a notebook [#from-a-notebook]

```python
semantic = nb.semantic_model(connection, "sales_360",
                             tables=["AMAZON.ORDER_LINES", "VS_LOGISTICS.COURIER_DAILY"],
                             links=["AMAZON.ORDER_LINES.SHIP_STATE=VS_LOGISTICS.STATE_LOGISTICS.STATE"],
                             preview=True)
semantic = semantic.publish()
nb.semantic_sql(connection, "SELECT ship_state, total_amount FROM SEM_SALES_360.ORDER_LINES GROUP BY ship_state")
nb.refresh_semantic(connection, "sales_360")
```

In the guided view, the **Semantic views** card in Understand does the same: pick the tables, let the AI propose the fields, preview, publish, refresh.

## Further reading [#further-reading]

* [exasol-labs/exasol-semantic-views](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-semantic-views), the add-on's repository and README.
* [What the kit writes](/security/what-the-kit-writes), which schemas the semantic models create, and which tables they never change.
* [What is sent to an AI model](/security/what-goes-to-a-model), the exact content of the `--ai` proposal.


# All exakit commands (/kit/reference/commands)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from setup/help/exakit.json. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

`exakit help <command>` prints a command's full reference on this computer, and `exakit catalog <word>`
searches them.

## Everyday [#everyday]

| Command            | Takes                                                                   | What it does                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `exakit status`    | `[--json]`                                                              | Is the database up and healthy?                                                 |
| `exakit info`      | `[--json]`                                                              | Your connection details.                                                        |
| `exakit start`     | `[<service>]`                                                           | Start the database and every add-on service, or one of them.                    |
| `exakit stop`      | `[<service>]`                                                           | Stop the add-on services and the database, or one of them.                      |
| `exakit sql`       | `'<statement>' \| --file <path> \| (stdin) [--json] [--write] [--help]` | Run one SQL statement, with the error translated.                               |
| `exakit data-load` | `[<file-or-folder-or-dataset>] [--force]`                               | Load a dataset (downloaded only when you pick it), one file, or a whole folder. |
| `exakit logs`      | `[<target>] [-f] [--lines N] [--path] [--json]`                         | Every log the kit can show.                                                     |
| `exakit autostart` |                                                                         | Come back automatically after a restart?                                        |

## AI clients (MCP) [#ai-clients-mcp]

| Command             | Takes                      | What it does                       |
| ------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `exakit mcp-setup`  |                            | Connect your AI clients.           |
| `exakit mcp-doctor` | `[clients] [--json]`       | Test and repair the AI connection. |
| `exakit mcp-status` | `[clients] [--json \| -j]` | Show managed MCP state per client. |

## External sources (virtual schemas) [#external-sources-virtual-schemas]

| Command          | Takes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | What it does                                                    |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `exakit connect` | `[source] [--name N] [--url STRING] [--set KEY=VALUE]... [--password-file F \| --password-stdin] [--storage-secret-file F] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--json]`                                                                                                                             | Query an external database from the local one (virtual schema). |
| `exakit source`  | `list\|issues [--status S]\|catalog\|show <name>\|describe <name> [TABLE] [--ddl] [--schema S]\|check <name>\|--all\|reauth <name> [--password-file F \| --password-stdin] [--storage-secret-file F]\|refresh <name>\|disconnect <name>\|remove <name> [--dry-run] [--yes] [--json]` | List, check and manage connected external sources.              |

## Personas and notebooks [#personas-and-notebooks]

| Command           | Takes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `exakit persona`  | `list \| show <id> \| plan [<id>] [--json] \| add [<id>[,<id>]] \| remove <id>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Who the kit is set up for - Data Scientist or General: list, show, plan, add or remove one.                                                                                                       |
| `exakit notebook` | `[jupyterlab \| marimo] [check] [setup] [stop] [--no-browser] [--port <number>]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Open JupyterLab or Marimo, connected to the local database (the notebook add-on).                                                                                                                 |
| `exakit describe` | `<SCHEMA.TABLE> [--sample <rows>] [--id <slug>] [--json] [--write <path>] \| <id\|SCHEMA.TABLE\|draft.yaml> --approve [--role <slot>=<COLUMN>]... [--owner <who>] [--no-comments] [--json] \| <id> --show [--version <n>] [--json] \| <id> --versions [--json] \| <id> --comments [--json] \| --schema <SCHEMA> [--approve [--link <TABLE.COLUMN>=<TABLE.KEY>]... [--unlink <TABLE.COLUMN>]... [--owner <who>] [--no-comments]] [--json] \| --model <NAME> --table <SCHEMA.TABLE>... [--link <SCHEMA.TABLE.COLUMN>=<SCHEMA.TABLE.KEY>]... [--ai] [--description <text>] [--dry-run] [--json] \| --model <NAME> --refresh [--json] \| --models [--json] \| --model <NAME> --schemas <A,B,C> [--find-links] [--ai] [--dry-run] [--json] \| --links <A,B[,C...]> [--ai] [--json]` | Draft each column's role in a table (key, time, measure, category, flag, text, identifier, other), approve it, and publish it as an Exasol Semantic Views model for the notebooks and AI clients. |
| `exakit workflow` | `list \| show <id> [--json \| -j]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | The workflow logs the notebook helpers write: list them, show one.                                                                                                                                |

## Models and UDFs (udf-devkit, hidden for now) [#models-and-udfs-udf-devkit-hidden-for-now]

| Command            | Takes                                                                                                                                          | What it does                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `exakit mlflow`    | `start\|stop\|disable\|status\|url\|replay [action options]`                                                                                   | Start or stop the local MLflow server, show its address, or replay pending runs.                                                 |
| `exakit udf-setup` | `[--language python\|rust] [--force] [--yes] [--json]`                                                                                         | Python or Rust UDFs: install the official Python container (or the pinned Rust one) and prove it (the udf-devkit add-on).        |
| `exakit udf-use`   | `default [--language python\|rust] [--yes] [--json] \| <container.tar.gz> [--alias NAME] [--language python\|rust] [--yes] [--json] \| --list` | Install a script language container: the kit's prebuilt one for this database, or a tarball of your own.                         |
| `exakit udf-build` | `<requirements.txt> [--alias <NAME>] [--yes]`                                                                                                  | Build a container with your pinned packages and install it.                                                                      |
| `exakit udf-file`  | `<file> [<path in the bucket>]`                                                                                                                | Copy a file into BucketFS and print the path a UDF reads it from.                                                                |
| `exakit rust-udf`  | `new <name> [--coefficients <file>] \| build <name> \| deploy <name> [--schema <SCHEMA>] [--yes] [--json]`                                     | Create, build and deploy a Rust scoring UDF from exported coefficients.                                                          |
| `exakit model`     | `put\|inspect\|list\|rm\|prune\|template [arguments]`                                                                                          | Model files in the bucket directory: put one (digest recorded, /buckets path printed), list them, find the scoring UDF template. |

## Add-ons [#add-ons]

| Command              | Takes                                | What it does                                                             |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `exakit marketplace` | `[<addon-id>...] \| --list [--json]` | Optional add-ons: dashboards, notebooks, UDFs, dbt, scheduling and more. |

## Keeping up to date [#keeping-up-to-date]

| Command          | Takes                            | What it does                          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `exakit version` | `[--json \| -j]`                 | What is installed, and what is newer. |
| `exakit update`  | `[<component>] [--yes] [--json]` | Apply the updates that are waiting.   |

## Repair and removal [#repair-and-removal]

| Command                 | Takes                                                                                                                              | What it does                                          |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `exakit preflight`      |                                                                                                                                    | Check this machine's requirements; install nothing.   |
| `exakit repair-runtime` | `[--yes] [--json \| -j]`                                                                                                           | Rebuild a database that cannot start.                 |
| `exakit tls-pin`        | `[--accept [--yes]] [--json \| -j]`                                                                                                | Compare or re-pin the database's TLS certificate.     |
| `exakit migrate`        | `docker-nano [--container NAME] [--engine docker\|podman] [--dsn HOST:PORT] [--user USER] [--password-file PATH] [--yes] [--json]` | Copy an older kit's container database into this one. |
| `exakit uninstall`      | `[<addon-id>] [--dry-run] [--yes]`                                                                                                 | Remove what the kit installed.                        |

## Reference [#reference]

| Command            | Takes                                                       | What it does                                  |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `exakit guide`     |                                                             | Friendly walkthrough of every way to connect. |
| `exakit skills`    | `[--json \| -j]`                                            | List the AI skills the kit carries.           |
| `exakit help`      | `[<component> \| <command> [<action>...]] [--all] [--json]` | This screen.                                  |
| `exakit catalog`   | `[search] [--json \| -j]`                                   | Browse or search every command.               |
| `exakit whats-new` | `[<version>]`                                               | What changed in this kit version.             |

## Other [#other]

| Command                 | Takes                    | What it does                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `exakit mcp-remove`     | `<client> [<client>...]` | Remove the kit's MCP entries from named AI clients.        |
| `exakit skills-install` |                          | Re-place the AI skills the kit copy carries (repair only). |
| `exakit upgrade-kit2`   |                          | Add the Kit 2 trust assets to this install (internal).     |
| `exakit rollback-kit2`  |                          | Remove exactly what upgrade-kit2 added (internal).         |


# Choose and change a persona (/kit/personas/choose-and-change)



## At install time [#at-install-time]

Name the persona on the install command:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://www.exasol.com/install/starter-kit.sh | EXAKIT_PERSONA=data-scientist sh
```

```bash
curl -fsSL https://www.exasol.com/install/starter-kit.sh | EXAKIT_PERSONA=data-scientist,general sh
```

Without `EXAKIT_PERSONA`, on a terminal, the installer asks three things after the parts everyone needs:

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### What will you use this machine for? [#what-will-you-use-this-machine-for]

    Tick as many personas as you like. General is ticked to begin with.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Data to load [#data-to-load]

    One table. The datasets of the personas you picked are ticked; the others are listed and can be ticked too. Your own file or folder and Skip are there as well.
  </Step>

  <Step>
    ### Add-ons for your personas [#add-ons-for-your-personas]

    Every add-on, with your personas' own ticked. Tick or untick any, then Enter installs what is ticked.
  </Step>
</Steps>

Nothing is loaded or installed without that screen. Without a terminal and without `EXAKIT_PERSONA`, the kit installs on its own with the General samples: TPC-H, energy and weather.

## On an installed kit [#on-an-installed-kit]

```bash
exakit persona list                  # the personas this kit has
exakit persona show data-scientist   # what one brings, and what to do first
exakit persona plan                  # what your personas bring, and what of it is still pending
exakit persona add general           # become that persona too
exakit persona remove general        # leave it
```

`plan` takes `--json` for a script.

## Add another persona to this kit [#add-another-persona-to-this-kit]

```bash
exakit persona add general
```

On a kit set up as Data Scientist this makes it both. Three steps run, headed like the installer's: sample data, AI clients, add-ons.

* What is already here is named in one line and not redone.
* A part that fails does not stop the others. The closing line names each part that did not finish and the command that retries it.
* At a terminal you can change the ticks before Enter. Without one, the same happens in plain lines.

## Remove a persona [#remove-a-persona]

```bash
exakit persona remove data-scientist
```

This removes only the membership from the kit's record. Datasets, notebooks and add-ons stay, because another persona or you may still use them. To remove an add-on, use `exakit uninstall <addon-id>`.

## Override one answer [#override-one-answer]

An answer you give yourself wins for that one variable:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://www.exasol.com/install/starter-kit.sh | EXAKIT_PERSONA=data-scientist EXAKIT_DATASETS=amazon_sales sh
```

This loads only the Amazon dataset and keeps the persona's AI clients and add-ons.

| Variable                    | Answers                                        |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `EXAKIT_PERSONA`            | Which personas, comma-separated                |
| `EXAKIT_DATASETS`           | Which datasets to load                         |
| `EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS` | Which add-ons to install: ids, `all` or `none` |
| `EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS`        | Which AI clients to connect                    |

<Callout>
  Use names, not menu numbers: `EXAKIT_DATASETS=tpch`, `EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS=claude,codex`.
</Callout>


# Define your own persona (/kit/personas/define-your-own)



A persona is one file, `personas/<id>.json`, in the kit's repository. No installer code names a persona, so adding a file is the whole change.

## Try it first [#try-it-first]

`tools/try_persona.sh` runs a persona in a sandbox that changes nothing. `personas/examples/analyst.json` is a ready-made one to start from.

```bash
bash tools/try_persona.sh personas/examples/analyst.json
```

```bash
bash tools/try_persona.sh personas/examples/analyst.json --ask
```

The first shows the checks, the question, the answers and the data table. The second then asks the install question live.

## The keys [#the-keys]

| Key                | Value                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schema_version`   | `1`                                                                                                                                |
| `id`               | The file name without `.json`                                                                                                      |
| `title`, `summary` | What `exakit persona list` and the install question show                                                                           |
| `picker`           | `true` to offer it in the install question                                                                                         |
| `visible`          | `true` to offer new selections. `false` hides it and refuses a new add, while keeping the definition and an existing installation. |
| `default`          | `true` to tick it to begin with                                                                                                    |
| `order`            | Where the question lists it, lowest first                                                                                          |
| `datasets`         | A list of dataset ids, or `"all"` or `"none"`                                                                                      |
| `mcp_clients`      | `"all"`, `"skip"`, or a list of client ids                                                                                         |
| `addons`           | A list of add-on ids, or `"all"` or `"none"`                                                                                       |
| `addon_reasons`    | Optional. One line per add-on, at most 90 characters, saying what it does for this persona                                         |
| `notebook_tools`   | Optional. Which notebook tools to tick, for example `["jupyterlab", "marimo"]`                                                     |
| `services`         | Optional. Kit services the persona starts at login, for example `["mlflow"]`                                                       |
| `udf_language`     | Optional. `python` or `rust`                                                                                                       |
| `first_prompt`     | Optional. What to do first, shown by `exakit persona show`                                                                         |

## Rules [#rules]

* **No secrets and no machine paths.** A persona names things, it never holds them.
* **It appears where `order` puts it** when `visible` and `picker` are true.
* **Its notebooks** go in `notebook/notebooks/<id>/`, listed in `notebook/catalog.json`.
* **Its documentation** goes in `notebook/docs/content/docs/<id>/`. See [These docs](/data-scientist/development/docs-site).

## Checks [#checks]

```bash
bash tests/personas.sh
```

It validates every persona file against the datasets and add-ons this kit ships. `tests/personas-ps.ps1` checks that the Windows side reads the files the same way.


# What is a persona (/kit/personas/what-is-a-persona)



A **persona** is a named set of answers to the questions the installer asks: which datasets to load, which AI clients to connect and which add-ons to install. Choosing a persona is choosing what this computer is for.

A persona names things. It never holds a secret or a path on your machine.

## The personas in this kit [#the-personas-in-this-kit]

| Persona                               | Datasets                             | Add-ons                   | First notebook                 |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| **Data Scientist** (`data-scientist`) | `amazon_sales`, `fraud_transactions` | `dash-server`, `notebook` | `data-scientist/00_quickstart` |
| **General** (`general`)               | `tpch`, `energy`, `weather`          | none                      | none                           |
| **ML Engineer** (`ml-engineer`)       | `amazon_sales`, `fraud_transactions` | `notebook`, `udf-devkit`  | `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`    |

Every persona connects all the AI clients found on this computer.

<Callout type="warn">
  ML Engineer is kept in the kit but **not offered in this release**. It cannot be newly selected. A kit that was set up with it before keeps working.
</Callout>

## What each one is for [#what-each-one-is-for]

**Data Scientist.** Four notebooks that take a table from loading to a shared dashboard: agree what each column means, prepare, explore, train a small model, ask questions in plain language and hand the work off. It gets the dashboard server first and then the notebooks, because the notebooks' Share step publishes a dashboard there. See [Data Scientist](/data-scientist).

**General.** The kit's own sample data and nothing else: a database to query with SQL or an AI client. Its datasets are bundled with the kit and load without internet.

**ML Engineer.** In-database training and scoring. It also starts a local MLflow server and installs the UDF runtime.

## Personas combine [#personas-combine]

Personas are not exclusive. Choosing two loads the datasets of both and installs the add-ons of both, each once. Choosing all of them gives you everything.

General is ticked to begin with in the install question, and combines with the others like any persona.

## What a persona does not do [#what-a-persona-does-not-do]

* It does not lock anything. Any dataset or add-on can be added later, whatever the persona.
* It does not remove anything when you leave it. Removing a persona only removes the membership; the data, notebooks and add-ons stay.

## Further reading [#further-reading]

* [User-defined functions (UDFs)](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/udf_scripts.htm) and [BucketFS](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/bucketfs/bucketfs.htm), the two parts of the UDF runtime that the ML Engineer persona uses.
* [exasol/exasol-personal](https://github.com/exasol/exasol-personal), the local database the kit deploys.
* [Add-ons](/kit/tools/add-ons), with each add-on's repository and documentation.

Next: [choose and change a persona](/kit/personas/choose-and-change).


# Add-ons (/kit/tools/add-ons)



Add-ons are optional tools around the database: dashboards, notebooks and more. A persona installs the ones it needs. You can add or remove any of them later.

## See what there is [#see-what-there-is]

```bash
exakit marketplace --list
```

Every add-on is listed with its state, its version and what it is. Nothing is installed. Add `--json` for a script.

The name, the link and the About text of an add-on come from its own repository on GitHub, as last looked up. When a lookup fails, the kit's own copy is shown.

## Install [#install]

```bash
exakit marketplace                 # choose in a menu: Space selects, Enter installs
exakit marketplace dash-server     # install exactly this one
```

<Callout>
  Without a terminal, a bare `exakit marketplace` installs nothing. Name the add-ons, or answer up front: `EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS=dash-server exakit marketplace`.
</Callout>

## Start, stop and check [#start-stop-and-check]

Some add-ons are services, such as the dashboard server.

```bash
exakit start dash-server
exakit stop dash-server
exakit status
exakit logs dash-server
```

`exakit start` with no name starts the database and every enabled add-on service.

After an install, `exakit status` shows whether a service add-on is running, and `exakit help <add-on>` prints its full reference.

## Update and remove [#update-and-remove]

```bash
exakit update                  # apply the updates that are waiting
exakit update notebook         # one component
exakit uninstall dash-server   # remove one add-on
```

`exakit uninstall` takes `--dry-run` to preview what would be removed.

## Help for one add-on [#help-for-one-add-on]

```bash
exakit help dash-server
```

The full reference of an installed add-on is on this computer.

## From a notebook [#from-a-notebook]

```python
nb.addons()                      # every add-on and its state
nb.addon_ready("dash-server")    # install it when missing, start it when stopped
nb.kit_update()                  # bring the kit and its add-ons up to date
```

The Home card's **Marketplace** tab does the same with buttons. See [Run the kit from a notebook](/data-scientist/set-up).

<Callout>
  A tool you installed yourself is recognised and never offered again.
</Callout>

## The add-ons [#the-add-ons]

Each entry gives what the add-on is (the one line the catalog holds), how the kit installs it, its repository, and its documentation. Where the kit pins a version or a SHA-256 digest for an add-on, [Add-ons and downloads](/security/add-ons-and-downloads) lists it.

### dash-server [#dash-server]

* **What it is:** Agent-operated Dash hosting for live analytical apps.
* **Install:** `exakit marketplace dash-server`
* **Repository:** [exasol-labs/dash-server](https://github.com/exasol-labs/dash-server)
* **Documentation:** [repository README](https://github.com/exasol-labs/dash-server#readme).

### dbt-exasol [#dbt-exasol]

* **What it is:** Data Build Tool adapter for Exasol.
* **Install:** `exakit marketplace dbt-exasol`
* **Repository:** [exasol/dbt-exasol](https://github.com/exasol/dbt-exasol)
* **Documentation:** [dbt's Exasol setup page](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/core/connect-data-platform/exasol-setup), and the [repository README](https://github.com/exasol/dbt-exasol#readme).

### exasol-scheduler [#exasol-scheduler]

* **What it is:** Lightweight table-driven SQL job scheduling for Exasol.
* **Install:** `exakit marketplace exasol-scheduler`
* **Repository:** [exasol-labs/exasol-scheduler](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-scheduler)
* **Documentation:** [repository README](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-scheduler#readme).

### exasol-vscode [#exasol-vscode]

* **What it is:** A Visual Studio Code extension for working with Exasol databases. Provides comprehensive database management, intelligent SQL editing, and powerful query execution capabilities.
* **Install:** `exakit marketplace exasol-vscode`. If you installed the extension yourself, the kit leaves it as yours and does not replace it.
* **Repository:** [exasol-labs/exasol-vscode](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-vscode)
* **Documentation:** [repository README](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-vscode#readme).

### json-tables [#json-tables]

* **What it is:** Exasol JSON Tables: ingest, query, and reshape JSON-shaped data in Exasol.
* **Install:** `exakit marketplace json-tables`
* **Repository:** [exasol-labs/exasol-json-tables](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-json-tables)
* **Documentation:** [repository README](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-json-tables#readme), and Exasol's [JSON functions](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/sql_references/functions/json.htm).

### semantic-views [#semantic-views]

* **What it is:** A database-native semantic layer for Exasol.
* **Install:** `exakit marketplace semantic-views`. The first approval of a column map installs it into the database if it is missing, as [Semantic Views](/kit/data/semantic-views) describes.
* **Repository:** [exasol-labs/exasol-semantic-views](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-semantic-views)
* **Documentation:** [repository README](https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-semantic-views#readme).

### notebook [#notebook]

* **What it is:** Connection configuration management and additional tools for Jupyter notebooks.
* **Install:** `exakit marketplace notebook`. It offers two front ends, JupyterLab and Marimo. See [Notebooks](/kit/tools/notebooks).
* **Repository:** [exasol/notebook-connector](https://github.com/exasol/notebook-connector)
* **Documentation:** [repository README](https://github.com/exasol/notebook-connector#readme). The driver the notebooks use is documented in Exasol's [PyExasol page](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/connect_exasol/drivers/python/pyexasol.htm).

### udf-devkit [#udf-devkit]

* **What it is:** Run Python and Rust code inside the database: UDF containers, model files in BucketFS, a local MLflow. The kit writes this line in place of its repository's About text, because the repository is the upstream it is built on.
* **Install:** Not available in this release. The catalog marks the add-on `visible: false`, and `exakit marketplace udf-devkit` refuses it with "is disabled in marketplace/catalog.json".
* **Repository:** [exasol/script-languages-release](https://github.com/exasol/script-languages-release). This is the upstream repository the kit builds its containers from.
* **Documentation:** Exasol's [user-defined functions](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/udf_scripts.htm), [Python in UDFs](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/udf_scripts/python3.htm), and [BucketFS](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/bucketfs/bucketfs.htm).


# AI clients and skills (/kit/tools/ai-clients-and-skills)



The kit connects AI clients to the database through its AI bridge. A client connected this way reads data as the kit's read-only user.

## Connect [#connect]

```bash
exakit mcp-setup
```

It configures the `exasol` MCP server in every supported AI client. Existing configs are backed up first. To name the clients yourself, set `EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS` before the command:

```bash
EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS=claude,codex exakit mcp-setup
```

Restart each client afterwards and look for a server named `exasol`.

## Check and repair [#check-and-repair]

```bash
exakit mcp-status      # the state of each client
exakit mcp-doctor      # test the connection and repair it
```

Both take `--json` for a script.

## Skills [#skills]

A **skill** is a set of instructions that teaches an AI client how to use the kit: which command loads data, how to read a column map, where dashboards go.

```bash
exakit skills              # the skills the kit carries
exakit skills-install      # put them back in place (repair)
```

Skills update with the kit, so a new skill reaches every installed kit through `exakit update`.

## What a client can and cannot do [#what-a-client-can-and-cannot-do]

* It reads through the read-only user. It cannot change your data.
* It reads the approved [column maps](/kit/data/column-maps), so it works from the roles you approved.
* The notebooks send a model names, types, notes and a column's most frequent values for most AI steps. One step sends row text: the themes step in Explore (`nb.themes`) sends the text column of sampled rows, up to 600 characters each, to sort them into themes. Every AI step is off until you set a model up. See [What goes to a model](/security/what-goes-to-a-model) and [AI and tracing](/data-scientist/set-up/ai-and-langfuse).

## From a notebook [#from-a-notebook]

```python
nb.ai_clients()                # the clients the kit can connect, and which are connected
nb.exakit("mcp-doctor")        # check the connection
```

## Further reading [#further-reading]

* [Exasol MCP server documentation](https://exasol.github.io/mcp-server/main/index.html), and its [repository](https://github.com/exasol/mcp-server). The kit runs this server beside the database and copies its skills.
* [Privileges](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/database_concepts/privileges.htm) and [GRANT](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/sql/grant.htm), the rules behind the read-only user.
* [AI clients and the read-only user](/security/ai-clients), the security view of the same connection, with its limits.


# Notebooks (/kit/tools/notebooks)



The notebook add-on brings JupyterLab and Marimo, the kit's notebooks and the helpers they use. Install it with a persona that has notebooks, or with `exakit marketplace notebook`.

## Open [#open]

```bash
exakit notebook                 # choose a tool on a terminal; JupyterLab otherwise
exakit notebook jupyterlab
exakit notebook marimo
```

It starts on this computer only and opens in your browser, already signed in. The kernel is **Exasol (Starter Kit)**.

Every run first writes the kit's current connection into the notebooks' encrypted store, so a database restart or a port change needs no edit. It also copies any kit notebook you do not have yet. Yours are never overwritten.

## Check, set up, stop [#check-set-up-stop]

```bash
exakit notebook check           # prove the connection; start nothing
exakit notebook setup           # settle JupyterLab; start nothing
exakit notebook stop            # stop both notebook servers
exakit notebook stop marimo     # stop only Marimo
exakit notebook marimo --no-browser --port 2720
```

## Where the notebooks are [#where-the-notebooks-are]

| Tool       | Folder                                                             |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| JupyterLab | `~/.exasol-starter-kit/notebooks/starter-kit-notebooks/<persona>/` |
| Marimo     | `~/.exasol-starter-kit/notebooks/marimo/<persona>/`                |

## What an update does to them [#what-an-update-does-to-them]

* A kit notebook you did not edit is refreshed when the kit's version changes.
* A notebook you edited is never overwritten.
* A notebook you deleted is not copied back.

## A notebook of your own [#a-notebook-of-your-own]

Put it in the same persona folder, named with the next step number and a short topic, for example `04_churn_by_region.ipynb`. Start it with:

```python
import exakit.nb as nb

connection = nb.connect()
```

## The documentation, from a notebook [#the-documentation-from-a-notebook]

```python
nb.docs()
```

See [Data Scientist](/data-scientist) for the four notebooks and their nine steps.

## Further reading [#further-reading]

* [exasol/notebook-connector](https://github.com/exasol/notebook-connector), the connection package the notebook add-on installs.
* [PyExasol](https://docs.exasol.com/db/latest/connect_exasol/drivers/python/pyexasol.htm), Exasol's documentation of the Python driver the notebooks connect with, and its [repository](https://github.com/exasol/pyexasol).
* [How the notebooks handle credentials and model keys](/security/credentials).


# Workflows (/kit/tools/workflows)



A notebook starts a **workflow** and gets an id such as `wf-20261027-3f9a1c`. While it is active, every step the helpers run adds one line to its log. For the idea, see [Workflow](/data-scientist/set-up).

## List [#list]

```bash
exakit workflow list
```

One row per workflow: its id, first and last time, number of lines and name.

## Show one [#show-one]

```bash
exakit workflow show wf-20261027-3f9a1c
```

Its lines in order. Each one is a step:

| Line                                 | What happened                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start`                              | The workflow began, with its name                                                   |
| `step`                               | A later notebook continued it                                                       |
| `sql`                                | A statement ran                                                                     |
| `describe.draft`, `describe.approve` | A column map was drafted or approved                                                |
| `ask.approve`, `ask.answer`          | A question's SQL was approved, and it answered                                      |
| `model`                              | A model was trained and scored                                                      |
| `trace`                              | A model call was traced                                                             |
| `dashboard.revision`                 | A dashboard was previewed or published                                              |
| `handoff`                            | A hand-off was written                                                              |
| `guide_action`                       | A button or form on a notebook card ran, with the code it ran and whether it worked |

Add `--json` to either command for a script.

## Where the logs are [#where-the-logs-are]

`~/.exasol-starter-kit/workflows/<id>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, readable by you only.

## No secrets [#no-secrets]

The helpers refuse a password, a token, a secret or an API key, and a connection string with a password in it. The log never holds a credential.

<Callout>
  The workflow log is written by the notebook helpers, so this command needs the notebook add-on: `exakit marketplace notebook`.
</Callout>


# Build the dashboard query (/data-scientist/communicate/dashboard-query)



A dashboard starts from one query. The notebook builds that query from the approved column map, so the group and the count follow the roles you approved and not a name you typed.

## The code [#the-code]

In `03_share`, the dataset's roles build the query. The group is the category, the count is named after the grain, and the title and name follow from both:

```python
GROUP_ROLE, GROUP_COLUMN = dataset.group_by()             # CATEGORY for amazon_sales
GROUP_HEADER, COUNT_HEADER = nb.name(GROUP_COLUMN), nb.count_name(dataset)
dashboard_title = TITLE or f"{dataset.id} by {GROUP_HEADER.lower()}"
dashboard_query = f"SELECT {GROUP_COLUMN} AS {GROUP_HEADER}, COUNT(*) AS {COUNT_HEADER} FROM {dataset.fact_table} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY {COUNT_HEADER} DESC"
dashboard_draft = nb.share(dataset, dashboard_query, dashboard_title, app_name, measure="count")
```

`dataset.group_by()` returns the category. When the dataset has no category, it uses the entity, and then the target. The notebook prints a line when that happens.

## What it produces for amazon_sales [#what-it-produces-for-amazon_sales]

* The query: `SELECT CATEGORY AS CATEGORY, COUNT(*) AS ORDER_LINES FROM AMAZON.ORDER_LINES GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY ORDER_LINES DESC`
* The title: "amazon_sales by category"
* The name: `amazon-sales-by-category`

The count is called `ORDER_LINES` because the column map's grain says "one row per order line". The name comes from the grain, through `nb.count_name`.

`TITLE` and `APP_NAME` at the top of the notebook replace the generated title and name. The name identifies the dashboard on Dash Server.

## Before anything is sent [#before-anything-is-sent]

The notebook prints the query and its digest first, so you can read the SQL before it goes anywhere. Nothing is sent to Dash Server until you run the next cell.

## Next [#next]

Build the preview and check it on [Preview, check, publish](/data-scientist/communicate/preview-check-publish). Back to [Communicate and deploy](/data-scientist/communicate).


# Deploying a model (/data-scientist/communicate/deploying-a-model)



## Deploying a model [#deploying-a-model]

The kit does not deploy a model from these notebooks.

* The lab's fitted model is kept only in your kernel. Nothing saves or serves it. See [Saving, MLflow and training in the database](/data-scientist/model/saving-and-mlflow).
* `nb.use_model` and `nb.forget_model` look like they are about a model, but they are about the AI model endpoint and the Langfuse keys. They do not save or delete a trained model.
* Scoring a model inside the database is the ML Engineer's path. It needs the udf-devkit add-on (`exakit marketplace udf-devkit`), which provides a Python container for training and scoring.
* `exakit model put <file>` copies a model file into the bucket folder that the database's functions read, and `exakit model list` shows what is there. `nb.model_list()` returns the same list in a notebook.
* The ML Engineer's training runs `nb.prepare_training`, which is described on the [model page](/data-scientist/model/saving-and-mlflow). It writes the coefficients of a trained logistic regression beside the training hand-off, so a scoring notebook can read them without MLflow.

If you need a model in production, that path is the one the kit has. The Data Scientist notebooks stop at the result, the dashboard and the hand-off.

Back to [Communicate and deploy](/data-scientist/communicate).


# The hand-off bundle (/data-scientist/communicate/hand-off-bundle)



## The hand-off bundle [#the-hand-off-bundle]

`nb.handoff_bundle(connection, dataset)` writes one folder to `~/.exasol-starter-kit/bundles/<workflow id>/`, with a zip beside it. It needs no Dash Server and holds no password. The folder is named after the workflow. A bundle made with no workflow is named after the dataset.

<Flow
  caption="From the approved roles to a folder a colleague can repeat"
  steps="[
  { title: &#x22;The approved column map&#x22;, text: &#x22;descriptor.yaml and the schema map, as approved&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/kit/data/column-maps&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Every query the workflow ran&#x22;, text: &#x22;queries.sql, each query with its SHA-256 and row count&#x22;, code: &#x22;handoff = nb.handoff_bundle(connection, dataset)&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;The log and the README&#x22;, text: &#x22;workflow.jsonl and README.md, which say what was approved and published&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;One folder and a zip&#x22;, text: &#x22;Nothing in it is a password&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;A colleague repeats the work&#x22;, text: &#x22;From the README, with the same column map and queries&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22; },
]"
/>

## What is in the bundle [#what-is-in-the-bundle]

| File              | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `README.md`       | What the data is, which column map version the numbers rest on, which questions were approved, which dashboards were previewed or published, which model traces were made, and how to repeat the work |
| `descriptor.yaml` | The approved column map, copied from the kit's store                                                                                                                                                  |
| `schema-map.json` | The approved schema map, when the schema has one                                                                                                                                                      |
| `queries.sql`     | Every distinct query the workflow ran, each with its SHA-256 and row count                                                                                                                            |
| `workflow.jsonl`  | The workflow log, as it is                                                                                                                                                                            |

For `amazon_sales`, the folder holds the approved column map, the queries the workflow ran, the workflow log and the README.

## Writing it [#writing-it]

```python
handoff = nb.handoff_bundle(connection, dataset)
```

Running it again for the same workflow replaces the folder and the zip. It is a snapshot. Nothing in it checks itself against the data later. The page on [A training hand-off that went stale](/data-scientist/monitor/stale-hand-off) describes the one check the kit makes, and the bundle has no such check.

## Repeating the work [#repeating-the-work]

A colleague follows the README:

1. Load the same table. For a kit dataset, run `exakit data-load <id>`.
2. Open the approved column map with `nb.dataset(connection, "<id>")`, or `exakit describe <id> --show`.
3. Run the statements in `queries.sql` in order.

Back to [Communicate and deploy](/data-scientist/communicate). Next: [The training hand-off](/data-scientist/communicate/training-hand-off).


# Communicate and deploy (/data-scientist/communicate)



Communicating a result means two things: showing the figures to people who will not open the notebook, and leaving enough behind that someone else can repeat the work. The kit does both. A dashboard goes up on Dash Server, a kit add-on that the notebook installs and starts for you. It goes up as a preview first, and only a person can publish it. The hand-off bundle is one folder and a zip, and it needs no server. The kit does not deploy a model from these notebooks. The page on deploying a model explains what exists and where it lives.

## The flow [#the-flow]

<Flow
  caption="A dashboard: preview first, publish only after you check it"
  steps="[
  { title: &#x22;One checked result&#x22;, text: &#x22;A query you have read, built from the approved roles&#x22;, code: &#x22;dashboard_draft = nb.share(dataset, dashboard_query, title, name, measure=\&#x22;count\&#x22;)&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/communicate/dashboard-query&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Preview on Dash Server&#x22;, text: &#x22;Built from the approved roles, with the query and its lineage&#x22;, code: &#x22;dashboard_draft.preview(dash_server)&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/communicate/preview-check-publish&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Exasol runs the query&#x22;, text: &#x22;As the kit's read-only user, through Dash Server's profile&#x22;, tone: &#x22;db&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;You check the figures&#x22;, text: &#x22;Categories and counts match the SQL. Filters update the charts and the table.&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/communicate/what-a-reader-sees&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Publish&#x22;, text: &#x22;Only after you confirm, the exact healthy preview is promoted&#x22;, code: &#x22;dashboard_draft.confirm(dash_server, figures_checked=True)&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/communicate/preview-check-publish&#x22; },
]"
/>

<Flow
  caption="The hand-off folder: what is in it and how a colleague uses it"
  steps="[
  { title: &#x22;The approved column map&#x22;, text: &#x22;descriptor.yaml, the roles and their versions&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/kit/data/column-maps&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Every query the work ran&#x22;, text: &#x22;queries.sql, each with its digest and row count&#x22;, code: &#x22;handoff = nb.handoff_bundle(connection, dataset)&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, href: &#x22;/data-scientist/communicate/hand-off-bundle&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;The log and a README&#x22;, text: &#x22;workflow.jsonl and README.md, which say what was approved and published&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;One folder and a zip&#x22;, text: &#x22;Under the kit's home. Nothing in it is a password.&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;A colleague repeats the work&#x22;, text: &#x22;From the README, with the same column map and queries&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22; },
]"
/>

## Where you do it [#where-you-do-it]

| Guided view                                                                              | Notebook code                                                                                                                                 | Terminal                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `03_share`: the **Share** card has the steps Dash Server, Preview, Publish and Hand off. | `03_share`: `nb.share`, `dashboard_draft.preview`, `dashboard_draft.confirm`, `nb.handoff_bundle`. `nb.dash_tools()` connects to Dash Server. | `exakit marketplace dash-server` installs the add-on. `exakit start dash-server` starts it. `exakit status --json` gives its address. `exakit workflow show <id>` lists the workflow's steps. The bundle has no command of its own. |

The publish step is off by default in `03_share`. `FIGURES_CHECKED = False` stops the publish. The cell tells you to "open the healthy preview and check the figures before promoting." Set it to `True` only after you have checked the preview.

## How we used it [#how-we-used-it]

The worked example is `amazon_sales`, a result that counts order lines by category. The notebook builds the query from the approved roles, previews it, and writes the hand-off folder. The steps are on [Build the dashboard query](/data-scientist/communicate/dashboard-query).

For `amazon_sales` the query is `SELECT CATEGORY AS CATEGORY, COUNT(*) AS ORDER_LINES FROM AMAZON.ORDER_LINES GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY ORDER_LINES DESC`. The descriptor records nine distinct values for `CATEGORY`. The chart groups the smallest categories as Other when more than eight rows are shown, so check that grouped figure against the SQL as well.

## What you have at the end [#what-you-have-at-the-end]

A dashboard, first as a preview and then, after you check it, as a live address that you keep with the workflow id. You also have one hand-off folder and its zip. The next step is to notice when the data, the column map or the model changes: [Monitor and iterate](/data-scientist/monitor).
