</Cards>

## What you have at the end [#what-you-have-at-the-end]

A local Exasol database that answers, the kit's notebooks ready to open, and a workflow that logs what you do. Next, load the data you will work on in [Get the data](/data-scientist/get-the-data).

<StageNav n="1" />


# Install the kit (/data-scientist/set-up/install)



Run the command for your system in a terminal. The first install deploys the database. It is usually done in under 2 minutes.

## The command [#the-command]

macOS and Linux (and WSL):

```sh
curl https://www.exasol.com/install/starter-kit.sh | sh
```

Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://www.exasol.com/install/starter-kit.ps1 | iex
```

## Choose the Data Scientist set [#choose-the-data-scientist-set]

To install the Data Scientist set of parts without the menus, name the persona. On macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl https://www.exasol.com/install/starter-kit.sh | EXAKIT_PERSONA=data-scientist sh
```

On Windows, set `$env:EXAKIT_PERSONA = "data-scientist"` before the `irm` line.

The Data Scientist persona loads two sample datasets, `amazon_sales` and `fraud_transactions`. It connects every AI client it finds on the machine, and it installs Dash Server and the notebook add-on.

Without the variable, an interactive install asks which persona you want. Choose Data Scientist. A persona is a named set of answers: which datasets, AI clients and add-ons you get. See [the kit's personas](/kit/personas/what-is-a-persona).

## What the install puts on this computer [#what-the-install-puts-on-this-computer]

* **A local Exasol database.** It runs in a container. The kit uses Docker when Docker is running, and Podman otherwise. The kit never installs or starts Docker itself.
* **exapump**, the command-line tool that loads data files and runs SQL.
* **pyexasol**, the Python driver the notebooks use.
* **A read-only AI connection.** The kit's MCP server gives AI clients read access to the database, as a database user that cannot write. Passwords stay in `~/.exasol-starter-kit/credentials/`. Connecting a client is covered in [the kit's AI page](/kit/tools/ai-clients-and-skills).
* **The notebook add-on.** It holds the notebooks' Python, JupyterLab, Marimo and the kernel named **Exasol (Starter Kit)**. The Data Scientist persona installs it.
* **Personas and sample data.** See the persona section above.
* **Agent skills** for AI clients, placed where CLI agents look (`~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`).

## Wait for the install to finish [#wait-for-the-install-to-finish]

While the install runs, `exakit status` answers `installing` and exits with code 3. Poll it until it reports running.

Re-running the installer is safe. It skips the steps that finished and retries the ones that failed.

Back to [Set up Exasol](/data-scientist/set-up). Next: [Open the notebooks](/data-scientist/set-up/open-the-notebooks).


# Open the notebooks (/data-scientist/set-up/open-the-notebooks)



The notebooks run in your browser, on the kit's own Python. Both JupyterLab and Marimo open with the kernel **Exasol (Starter Kit)**. That kernel knows where the kit's database connection is, so no notebook asks for a host, a user or a password.

## Start them [#start-them]

```sh
exakit notebook             # JupyterLab, in your browser
exakit notebook marimo      # Marimo, in your browser
exakit notebook stop        # stop both servers
```

Run `exakit notebook` again after an install or an update to check the notebook environment and the database connection. It fixes what it can and says what it cannot fix.

## Run the notebooks in order [#run-the-notebooks-in-order]

Your copies are in `~/.exasol-starter-kit/notebooks/starter-kit-notebooks/data-scientist/`. Run them in this order:

1. `00_quickstart`
2. `01_explore`
3. `02_ask_your_data`
4. `03_share`

A notebook you edited is never overwritten by an update. A notebook you deleted is not copied back.

## The guided card and the Code view [#the-guided-card-and-the-code-view]

Each notebook opens with a guided card. A card has buttons and forms for the page's steps. The first card has a **Docs** button beside the logo. It opens this documentation on the page for that notebook.

Every card has a **Guided / Code** switch. **Guided** is the default. **Code** shows the calls behind each button. [Two ways through each notebook](/data-scientist#two-ways-through-each-notebook) explains both.

## Read these docs from a notebook [#read-these-docs-from-a-notebook]

```python
import exakit.nb as nb

nb.docs()                  # this site, under the cell
nb.docs("descriptor")      # search it
nb.docs(nb.describe)       # one command's page
nb.docs(browser=True)      # in a browser tab instead
```

The site ships with the kit and is served from this computer. Reading and searching work without internet.

If `nb.docs()` reports that the site is missing, run `nb.exakit("update", "notebook")`. More on this in [Troubleshooting](/data-scientist/set-up/troubleshooting).

Back to [Set up Exasol](/data-scientist/set-up). Next: [Check the kit](/data-scientist/set-up/check-the-kit).


# Troubleshooting (/data-scientist/set-up/troubleshooting)



Each entry gives the message or the symptom, then the command to run. The AI entries are at the end.

## Install and the command line [#install-and-the-command-line]

<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="exakit: command not found">
    The command is in `~/.local/bin`, and that folder is not on a bare shell's `PATH`. This does not mean the kit is missing. Run `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`, or call `~/.local/bin/exakit` by its full path. On Windows, call `exakit.cmd`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="exakit status says installing, or the installer stopped">
    `installing` with exit code 3 means the install is still running. Poll `exakit status` until it reports running. If the status names a re-run instead, the installer stopped. Run the installer again. It resumes where it stopped.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The database does not answer">
    ```python
    nb.kit_check()          # is the database running?
    nb.exakit("start")      # start it, for example after a restart of this computer
    ```

    `exakit status` also tells you what to run. If it says `interrupted`, do not loop on `exakit start`. Run `exakit repair-runtime` only after you have agreed to it: it rebuilds the database, and that destroys the data you loaded. The bundled datasets are loaded again afterwards. The kit asks before it does this.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="An add-on is missing or stopped">
    ```python
    nb.addon_ready("dash-server")
    ```

    It installs the add-on when it is missing and starts it when it is stopped.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="After an update, nothing changed">
    A running kernel keeps the helpers it loaded before the update. Restart the kernel. In JupyterLab, choose **Kernel**, then **Restart Kernel**.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Notebooks and docs [#notebooks-and-docs]

<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="The notebooks say the port is in use">
    Port 8888 (JupyterLab) or 2718 (Marimo) belongs to another program. Without `--port`, the kit uses the next free port and says which one. To pick a port yourself, run `exakit notebook --port 8890`. A port you name is refused when it is taken.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="JupyterLab or Marimo is missing from the kit">
    Run `exakit notebook setup`. It installs the kit's JupyterLab again at its pinned version. Without a terminal it does this without asking. If the notebook environment itself is broken, run `exakit update notebook`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The kernel Exasol (Starter Kit) is gone from Jupyter">
    Run `exakit notebook setup`. Every `exakit notebook` command registers the kernel again.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The browser does not open">
    Run `exakit notebook --no-browser`. It prints the address. The login token is in `~/.exasol-starter-kit/credentials`. Do not paste the token anywhere else.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A notebook cannot connect">
    Run `exakit notebook check`. It finds the kit's database connection and checks it.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The documentation does not open">
    `nb.docs()` reads the copy of the site in the kit. If it reports the site is missing, run `nb.exakit("update", "notebook")`. The site is served on this computer at one of the ports 8790 to 8809, the first one free. To choose the port, set `EXAKIT_DOCS_PORT` before you start the notebooks. If the notebook runs on another machine than your browser, the page cannot reach the site. Use `nb.docs(browser=True)` on the machine that runs the kit.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How do I find a command?">
    `nb.docs("words")` searches these docs. `nb.docs(nb.some_command)` opens that command's page. The [command reference](/data-scientist/development/reference) lists every helper.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Files and updates [#files-and-updates]

<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="Do I need a terminal?">
    No. Everything the notebooks need runs from a cell or a card: `nb.kit_check()`, `nb.exakit(...)`, `nb.addon_ready(...)`. You need a terminal once, to run the installer and open the notebooks.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Where is my work saved?">
    Under `~/.exasol-starter-kit`: column maps, workflow logs, hand-off bundles and the kit's credentials. The data you load lives in the database on this computer.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Will an update overwrite my notebooks?">
    No. A notebook you edited is never overwritten. A notebook you deleted is not copied back.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## AI model and tracing [#ai-model-and-tracing]

These entries are about the optional model and Langfuse settings. The setup steps are in [Set up AI and Langfuse](/data-scientist/set-up/ai-and-langfuse).

<Accordions type="multiple">
  <Accordion title="A model step is skipped">
    Either no model is set, or the dataset has no column for that step. Run `nb.model_settings()` to see what is set. Set the model as shown on [Set up AI and Langfuse](/data-scientist/set-up/ai-and-langfuse). The themes step also skips on a dataset with no text column, and says so. The reference datasets, `amazon_sales` and `fraud_transactions`, have no text column.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The message says the model is not usable">
    The settings are refused before any call is made. The message names the setting. Common causes:

    * The base URL is `http://` to a host outside this computer and your network. Use the provider's `https://` address.
    * The base URL includes a path such as `/chat/completions`, a query, or a username and password. Remove them. Give only the API base, such as `/v1/`.
    * `EXAKIT_PROVIDER_HEADERS` is not a JSON object of plain values, or it sets an authorization header. Put the key in `EXAKIT_PROVIDER_API_KEY` instead.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Langfuse says tracing is off">
    The message names the missing setting. Tracing needs all three: the public key, the secret key and the base URL. A plain `http://` address to a host outside this computer and your network also turns tracing off. Use the `https://` address.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I changed a setting and nothing changed">
    The notebook server read its environment when it started. Run `exakit notebook stop`, then `exakit notebook` from the terminal that has the variables. A kernel restart does not read them again, and a new terminal does not reach a server that is already running.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Do I need an AI model?">
    No. Every step runs without one. A model is used only to draft SQL in Ask and to sort texts into themes in Explore. Both are off until you turn them on. Ask also has a drafter that needs no model: `nb.draft_question`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Is my data sent anywhere?">
    Not by default. The database and the notebooks run on this computer. With a model set up, Ask sends the column map and your question, never rows. The themes step sends a sample of texts. It asks first when the data is a live external source. With Langfuse Cloud on, the recorded inputs and outputs of each model call are sent to Langfuse.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Can an AI-drafted query change my data?">
    No. Nothing runs until you approve the exact text. Approved questions run as the read-only user, and writes are rejected by the database.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

Back to [Set up Exasol](/data-scientist/set-up). Next stage: [Get the data](/data-scientist/get-the-data).


# Workflows (/data-scientist/set-up/workflows)



## Workflows [#workflows]

A **workflow** is one id that every query and decision in a piece of work carries. The quickstart starts it, and every later notebook continues it, so you never paste an id.

<Flow
  caption="A notebook session starts a workflow, and every step is logged"
  steps="[
  { title: &#x22;The first cell checks the kit&#x22;, text: &#x22;It changes nothing&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22;, code: &#x22;nb.kit_check()&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;The workflow cell starts a workflow&#x22;, text: &#x22;Every query and decision is under this id&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22;, code: &#x22;workflow_id = nb.workflow(\&#x22;data-scientist-quickstart\&#x22;)&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;Each step writes a log line&#x22;, text: &#x22;SQL, approvals, model calls, dashboards, the hand-off&#x22;, tone: &#x22;kit&#x22; },
  { title: &#x22;You read the log&#x22;, text: &#x22;A file on this computer, readable by you only&#x22;, tone: &#x22;you&#x22;, code: &#x22;nb.workflow_log(workflow_id)&#x22; },
]"
/>

## Start and continue [#start-and-continue]

```python
workflow_id = nb.workflow("data-scientist-quickstart")   # in the quickstart
nb.continue_workflow("explore")                          # in every later notebook
```

`nb.continue_workflow` takes the workflow of this kernel, or else the last one started on this computer. It starts a new one only when there is none. Nothing is logged without an active workflow, and the kit never starts one on its own.

## The workflow log [#the-workflow-log]

While a workflow is active, each helper that does something adds one line to its log. That includes a SQL statement, a column-map draft or approval, a model call and its trace, a dashboard revision and a hand-off. Every guided card action is a line too, with the code it ran and whether it worked.

The log is one file per workflow: `~/.exasol-starter-kit/workflows/<id>.jsonl`. Each line is a JSON object. The file is append-only and readable by you only. Ids look like `wf-20261027-3f9a1c`.

```python
nb.list_workflows()              # every workflow on this computer
nb.workflow_log(workflow_id)     # one workflow's events
nb.current_workflow()            # the id this kernel is using
```

```sh
exakit workflow show wf-20261027-3f9a1c
```

## What is never written [#what-is-never-written]

* A value named like a secret is refused before anything is written.
* A connection string with a password is refused too.
* SQL that looks credential-bearing, such as a statement with a `PASSWORD` or `API_KEY` column, is logged with its text replaced. Its digest is kept, and a warning is shown.
* A log that cannot be written warns, and the cell goes on. Logging never stops the work it describes.

The kit never writes a key into a cell, the code view or the log.

Back to [Set up Exasol](/data-scientist/set-up). Next: [Set up AI and Langfuse](/data-scientist/set-up/ai-and-langfuse).


# Ask your data (/data-scientist/development/reference/ask)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

The archived Governed SQL server is not installed. The kit's own model endpoint can draft SQL from an approved
descriptor; no SQL runs until the person approves it. The SQL runs on the launcher's MCP server beside the
database (the sidecar, on loopback), which connects as the dedicated read-only user only - never the notebook's
admin connection or an admin fallback. The notebook sends no password: the sidecar holds the read-only login.

## nb.ask [#ask]

```python
nb.ask(
    dataset: Any,
    question: str,
    proposed_sql: str | None=None,
    *,
    table_description: str | None=None,
    request_timeout: float | None=None,
    max_output_tokens: int | None=None,
    conn=None,
) -> Proposal
```

Draft SQL from the user's opted-in model endpoint; `proposed_sql` supports manual drafting.

With `conn` (the notebook's connection) and a semantic model the kit built over this data, the model answers
from the semantic layer: it is shown the model's metrics and dimensions, writes Semantic SQL over the published
view, and Exasol Semantic Views compiles that into the plain SQL you read and approve - the same definitions an
AI client over MCP uses, so both give the same number. Without a model over the data, or when the question
cannot be put in its terms, the SQL is drafted from the approved column map as before, and the proposal says so.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/02_ask_your_data`

## nb.Proposal [#Proposal]

```python
class nb.Proposal
```

A question with the SQL proposed for it. Nothing runs until `approve()` accepts that exact text; `edit()` replaces
the SQL and removes the approval; `run()` runs the approved text through the kit's read-only service.

| Member                       | What it is  |
| ---------------------------- | ----------- |
| `dataset`                    | `Any`       |
| `question`                   | `str`       |
| `sql`                        | `str`       |
| `assumptions`                | `list[str]` |
| `doubts`                     | `list[str]` |
| `edit(sql: str) -> Proposal` |             |
| `approve() -> Proposal`      |             |
| `run()`                      |             |


# ML Engineer checks (/data-scientist/development/reference/checks)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

The three things the ML Engineer's notebooks depend on, one check each (ml-engineer/00_quickstart): the database's
Python container answers a smoke UDF with the packages training needs, the MLflow server is reachable, and the bucket
directory is where the kit expects it. Each prints one line - `ok` with what it found, or `FAIL` with the reason
and the fix - and returns True or False, so the notebook shows all three before anything stops.

Nothing here prints a host, a user or a password; an MLflow address is shown without any credentials it holds.

## nb.check_bucket [#check_bucket]

```python
nb.check_bucket(conn=None) -> bool
```

The deployment's bucket directory exists on this machine where the kit says it is, and - given a connection -
a UDF sees it at its /buckets path too (skipped, with a note, when the container check fails).

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`

## nb.check_container [#check_container]

```python
nb.check_container(
    conn,
    alias: str | None=None,
    packages: tuple[str, ...]=TRAINING_PACKAGES,
) -> bool
```

The container behind `alias` runs a smoke UDF, and it has every package training needs. The line names the
alias probed and the fix for that alias (PYTHON3_ML: exakit udf-use default; PYTHON3: exakit udf-setup), so the
fix installs the container the check looks at. `alias` None is the notebook's default, ml_train.udf_container():
PYTHON3_ML before PYTHON3 from the kit's manifest, EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINER first; none installed is a FAIL line.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`

## nb.check_mlflow [#check_mlflow]

```python
nb.check_mlflow(timeout: float=5.0) -> bool
```

Check the destination runs will really use: configured server, kit server, or local store.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`

## nb.check_model_compatibility [#check_model_compatibility]

```python
nb.check_model_compatibility(
    conn,
    model_version: str,
    alias: str='PYTHON3',
    model_path: str='model.pkl',
) -> bool
```

Refuse a pickle whose scikit-learn version differs before any scoring SQL runs.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.model_list [#model_list]

```python
nb.model_list(timeout: float=120.0) -> dict[str, Any]
```

What `exakit model list --json` says: bucket_dir (the host folder), udf_root (the path UDFs read it under) and
the models in it. Raises RuntimeError naming why it could not be read.


# Connect, SQL and tracing (/data-scientist/development/reference/core)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

The connection comes from the kit. Its Jupyter kernel ("Exasol (Starter Kit)") carries two paths: the encrypted
configuration store, and the kit's credential file holding the store's master password, readable by the user only.
These helpers open the database from there, in JupyterLab, Marimo, VS Code or any front end that runs the
kit's notebook Python. Nothing here prints or returns a host, a user or a password.

```python
import exakit.nb as nb
conn = nb.connect()
df = nb.sql(conn, "SELECT * FROM TPCH.NATION")
nb.show_sql()
ds = nb.dataset(conn, "amazon_sales")               # the roles of a dataset, checked against the database
ds = nb.load_own_file("~/data/sales.json", "MY_DATA.SALES", {"entity": "CUSTOMER", ...})   # or your own file
with nb.trace(conn, dataset=ds): ...              # model calls as one trace in your Langfuse (opt-in)
```

The quickstarts' shared steps (check_connection, list_schemas, load_sample, load_source, ...) are in quickstart.py;
the ML Engineer's checks (check_container, check_mlflow, check_bucket) in checks.py.

## nb.confirm_send [#confirm_send]

```python
nb.confirm_send(ds: Dataset, rows: int, answer: str | None=None) -> bool
```

Before sampled rows go to a model endpoint: True at once for a table in the database; for a live source (the
descriptor names a source) it names the source and asks, and only a yes sends. `answer` answers for a script;
with no one to ask (a headless run) the answer is no.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`

## nb.connect [#connect]

```python
nb.connect(**kwargs: Any)
```

A pyexasol connection to the local database, opened from the kit's encrypted store, pinned to the database's
TLS certificate once the kit has recorded it. Exasol's usage telemetry stays off unless EXASOL_TELEMETRY_DISABLE
was already set.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`, `data-scientist/02_ask_your_data`, `data-scientist/03_share`, `ml-engineer/01_train`, `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`, `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.model_client [#model_client]

```python
nb.model_client()
```

(client, model ID) for EXAKIT_MODEL_ID and EXAKIT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL; EXAKIT_PROVIDER_API_KEY is optional for
servers without authentication. Tracing uses Langfuse's instrumented client for the same endpoint and key.
This interface makes text Chat Completions calls; it does not provide a provider's native API features.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`

## nb.model_settings [#model_settings]

```python
nb.model_settings() -> dict
```

Display the chosen model and endpoint without the API key or custom header values; makes no request.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.show_sql [#show_sql]

```python
nb.show_sql() -> None
```

Print the last statement sql() ran, so a result can always be traced to the query behind it.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`, `data-scientist/01_explore`, `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`

## nb.sql [#sql]

```python
nb.sql(conn, statement: str, params: dict | None=None)
```

Run a query and return its rows as a pandas DataFrame; the statement is remembered for show_sql().

The rows come over the normal connection rather than pyexasol's HTTP export, which needs the database to connect
back to this machine - not a given through the local VM or Podman.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`, `data-scientist/01_explore`, `ml-engineer/00_quickstart`, `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`, `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.trace [#trace]

```python
nb.trace(
    conn,
    name: str='exakit-notebook',
    dataset: Dataset | None=None,
    sql: str | None=None,
    **metadata: Any,
) -> Iterator[Any]
```

Group the model calls made inside the block into one trace in the user's own Langfuse project, tagged with the
database session, the sample SQL, the workflow id and, given a dataset, its id, descriptor digest and descriptor
version (trace_tags). Opt-in: without LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_BASE_URL (LANGFUSE_HOST,
the SDK 3/4 name, still counts) it says so in one line and does nothing else - no exception, no prompt.

Langfuse SDK 5: the block is one observation (`Langfuse.start_as_current_observation`) and, right inside it, the
trace name, session id, tags and metadata are propagated (`langfuse.propagate_attributes`, a module function in
SDK 5) to it and to every observation opened within, so each call the client model_client() returns makes -
Langfuse's OpenAI drop-in when tracing is on - lands in this one trace with its input, output, token usage and
latency, without changes to the calling code. The span is yielded; the client is flushed when the block ends.
The active workflow's log gets one `trace` line with the trace id (X-1), and when the block ends one line is
printed - `traced: <trace id> (<url or base URL>)` - so the trace can be found in Langfuse. Nothing here prints
or records the secret key.

## nb.tracing [#tracing]

```python
nb.tracing() -> bool
```

Whether LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_BASE_URL (or LANGFUSE_HOST) are all set, so trace()
records to the user's Langfuse.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`


# Dash Server tools (/data-scientist/development/reference/dash-mcp)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

## nb.dash_tools [#dash_tools]

```python
nb.dash_tools(ready: bool=True) -> DashTools
```

The notebook's Dash Server tool adapter; each call is an MCP tool call. When Dash Server is not installed or
not running, it is installed and started first, the way nb.addon_ready("dash-server") does it (`exakit
marketplace dash-server`, `exakit start dash-server`), with its progress shown: a cell that previews a dashboard
works on its own, and nothing is asked. `ready=False` only reports: it raises when the server is not there.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/03_share`

## nb.DashTools [#DashTools]

```python
class nb.DashTools
```

Synchronous adapter for notebook cells, which already run an event loop.


# Data checks (/data-scientist/development/reference/data-checks)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

Both are built from the descriptor alone - the key, the label and every column's role - so no column name is typed in
a notebook and the same cell runs on every dataset. Each check is one or two SQL statements, run through nb.sql (so
they are shown and logged like every other query), and each finding is one plain sentence saying what it does to a
result. Nothing is changed in the data: deciding what to do about a finding is the user's.

```python
findings = nb.data_checks(conn, ds)        # Prepare: repeated keys and ids, exact copies, gaps, placeholders, a rare label
leaks = nb.leakage_check(conn, ds)         # Validate: columns whose values (almost) decide the label on their own
```

## nb.data_checks [#data_checks]

```python
nb.data_checks(conn, ds, *, show: bool=True)
```

Prepare: one row per finding - CHECK, COLUMN_NAME, ROWS_AFFECTED, PCT, MEANS - for repeated keys, repeated
identifiers, exact copies of a row, empty cells, placeholder values and a rare label. Prints each finding in one
sentence (`show=False` only returns them); an empty frame means the table passed every check.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`

## nb.leakage_check [#leakage_check]

```python
nb.leakage_check(conn, ds, *, show: bool=True) -> list[str]
```

Validate: the columns whose values (almost) decide the label on their own - each a value or values where the
label is (nearly) always 1 or always 0, covering most rows. Such a column is usually written after the outcome
(an order's status once it was cancelled) and makes any model look perfect; leave it out of the features. Returns
those columns (none: the list is empty) and prints why each was flagged.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`


# Data map (/data-scientist/development/reference/data-map)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
data = nb.data_map(connection)      # sample datasets, your loaded files and folders, connected sources
data                                # one table per origin: rows, columns, column map, roles; then the links
data.tables                         # one row per table (a DataFrame)
data.columns                        # one row per column, with its approved role when there is one
data.links                          # joins across tables and origins: declared, found, or a shared key name
```

Three origins, one view:

* \*\*sample\*\*: a dataset the kit ships (`exakit data-load amazon_sales`);
* \*\*local\*\*: your own file or folder (`exakit data-load <path>`, the quickstart's MY_DATA cell);
* \*\*source\*\*: a connected external source, read live through its virtual schema (`exakit connect`).

Roles come from the approved column maps in the kit's store, and the semantic layer is Exasol Semantic Views: a table
that is an entity of a semantic model the kit built says which model (SEMANTIC_CATALOG.ENTITIES). The links are the
approved schema maps' and the multi-source models' (nb.semantic_model). Columns that share a key-like name across
two tables are listed as possible links: a lead to check, never a join made for you. Only metadata is read.

## nb.data_map [#data_map]

```python
nb.data_map(conn, *, include_kit: bool=False) -> DataMap
```

The semantic map of the database: every table by origin (sample, local, source) with its rows, columns,
column-map state and roles, then the links between tables - declared, found by an approved schema map, or a
shared key-like column name across two tables (marked possible). Reads metadata only; returns a DataMap that
shows itself as a table in a notebook. `include_kit` keeps the kit's own schemas in.

## nb.DataMap [#DataMap]

```python
class nb.DataMap
```

What data_map found: tables, columns and links, each a list of dicts; DataFrames through the properties.

| Member                               | What it is                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table_rows`                         | `list[dict[str, Any]]`                                                          |
| `column_rows`                        | `list[dict[str, Any]]`                                                          |
| `link_rows`                          | `list[dict[str, Any]]`                                                          |
| `tables`                             |                                                                                 |
| `columns`                            |                                                                                 |
| `links`                              |                                                                                 |
| `table(name: str) -> dict[str, Any]` | One table's row, by SCHEMA.TABLE (any case).                                    |
| `roles(name: str) -> dict[str, str]` | \{column: role} of one table's approved column map; empty when it has none yet. |


# Datasets (/data-scientist/development/reference/dataset)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
ds = nb.dataset(conn, "amazon_sales")                 # a dataset the kit ships, by id
ds = nb.dataset(conn, "~/data/descriptor.yaml")    # a table already in the database, described by a descriptor file
ds = nb.dataset(conn, "~/data/sales.csv")          # your own CSV, Parquet or JSON file, its descriptor beside it
ds.col("label"), ds.text_sql(), ds.fact_table, ds.source
ds.version, ds.status, ds.owner, ds.created, ds.table_digest    # the descriptor's record (schema_version 2)
ds.require_approved("training")                    # a draft stops here with how to approve it
```

The rules are the kit's descriptor rules (`descriptor_rules`, shipped with this package: the 0.2 kit has no Python
package to import them from). It is a copy of tools/descriptor_rules.py, which tools/dataset_check.py uses, and
tests/test_notebook_contents.py holds the two byte-identical. Nothing is guessed: a descriptor that is invalid, or
names a table or column the database lacks, stops the notebook with the reason.

Which descriptor a name resolves to, in order: a path given (a file, or a folder holding descriptor.yaml); for a
data file of your own, `<name>.descriptor.yaml` beside it; for an id, the approved version in the kit's store
(`~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<SCHEMA>.<TABLE>/current.yaml`, or an older kit's `descriptors/<id>/current`;
descriptor_store), then the descriptor the kit ships under
`data/datasets/<id>/`. `ds.descriptor_path` and `ds.descriptor_origin` say which one was used.

## nb.chosen_dataset [#chosen_dataset]

```python
nb.chosen_dataset(name: str | Path | None=None) -> str
```

The dataset a notebook works on: `name` when it is set; with None, the one approved last in a quickstart (so
picking fraud_transactions there carries on here), else amazon_sales. Says which, and why, in one line.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/01_explore`, `data-scientist/02_ask_your_data`, `data-scientist/03_share`, `ml-engineer/01_train`, `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`, `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.Dataset [#Dataset]

```python
class nb.Dataset
```

A validated descriptor whose every role the database holds, with the SQL names the notebooks build queries from.

| Member                                      | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                                        | `str`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `path`                                      | `Path`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `digest`                                    | `str`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `descriptor`                                | `Any`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `descriptor_path`                           | \`Path                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | None\` |
| `descriptor_origin`                         | `str`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `fact_table`                                | `SCHEMA.TABLE` that one row of analysis comes from.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `source`                                    | The external source's alias when the table is in a virtual schema (a live source), else None - what confirm_send and the quickstart ask about.                                                                                                                  |
| `source_ref`                                | The descriptor's `source` as written: a dataset id, `file:<path>`, `vs:<alias>` (or a schema_version 1 file's bare alias), or None.                                                                                                                             |
| `version`                                   | The descriptor's version: 1 for a first draft or a shipped file; approving writes the next.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `status`                                    | `draft` (proposed, not yet confirmed) or `approved`.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `owner`                                     | Who drafted or approved it (`kit` for a shipped descriptor).                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `created`                                   | When this version was written (ISO-8601), None for a schema_version 1 file.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `table_digest`                              | The digest of the table the descriptor was approved on (its `digest` key, design 2.3: sha256 over the table's name, its columns and types, the row count and an order-independent content hash of the role columns), None until approve computes it.            |
| `current_table_digest(conn) -> str`         | The table's digest as it is now, computed the way approve computed `table_digest`; a value that differs from `table_digest` means the data changed since the descriptor was approved (a virtual table's digest covers its first sample rows and the row count). |
| `drafted_by`                                | `profile` (exakit describe), `shipped` (the kit) or `user` (roles given by hand).                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `evidence`                                  | Per role, the numbers that chose its column (what the profiler recorded; empty for roles given by hand).                                                                                                                                                        |
| `notes`                                     | Per column, a model-written line about it (never decisive; empty without a model).                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `missing`                                   | The roles no column fits, each `{role, reason}`; the notebooks skip what depends on them with the reason.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `require_approved(purpose: str) -> Dataset` | This dataset when its descriptor is approved; a draft raises DescriptorNotApproved saying how to approve it.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `col(role: str) -> str`                     | The column of a single-column role (entity, category, date, label).                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `text_cols() -> list[str]`                  | The text columns, in the descriptor's order; none when no column plays the text role.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `text_sql() -> str`                         | One SQL expression joining the text columns with a space, NULLs as empty; a dataset without text raises ValueError with the descriptor's reason.                                                                                                                |
| `roles() -> list[tuple[str, str]]`          | (role, SCHEMA.TABLE.COLUMN) for every role, for a table the notebook prints.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `has(role: str) -> bool`                    | Whether a column plays `role` (False for one listed under `missing`).                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `group_by() -> tuple[str, str]`             | (role, column) the overviews count rows by: the category, else the entity, else the target - a table with only a key, a text and a 0/1 target has no other group, and counting by that target is its overview.                                                  |
| `tags() -> dict[str, str]`                  | What a trace or an MLflow run records about the data: the dataset and the descriptor's digest (and the source's alias for a live source).                                                                                                                       |

## nb.dataset [#dataset]

```python
nb.dataset(conn, name: str | Path) -> Dataset
```

The dataset `name`, checked against the database: a kit dataset id, a descriptor file or its folder, or a data
file of your own (CSV, Parquet or JSON) with its descriptor beside it, which is loaded first (load_own_file).

**Used in:** `data-scientist/02_ask_your_data`, `data-scientist/03_share`, `ml-engineer/01_train`, `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`, `ml-engineer/03_score_external_model`

## nb.DescriptorNotApproved [#DescriptorNotApproved]

```python
exception nb.DescriptorNotApproved
```

A step that needs an approved descriptor was given a draft; the message says how to approve it.


# Describe a table (/data-scientist/development/reference/describe)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
d = exakit_nb.describe("AMAZON.ORDER_LINES")    # profile, draft v(n+1), show the table
d.set(PRODUCT="category", ZIP_CODE="identifier")  # corrections, chainable
d.slot(target="TIMELY_RESPONSE")                  # target=None leaves it empty on purpose
ds = d.approve()                                  # check, write, publish; the Dataset read back
```

describe() on a table whose approved descriptor still matches it returns that one (force=True profiles again);
otherwise the table is profiled once, in SQL, and every column gets one of eight roles with the evidence that chose
it; the slots name the columns the notebooks use. show() lists each column with the schema and table it came from,
its type, role, confidence, evidence and note, low confidence first, the slots above (rows() gives the same as dicts;
a notebook renders it as a table). approve() checks every column has a role and none sits in two slots, checks
the table has not changed since it was profiled, writes the next version into the kit's store and rebuilds the
schema's Exasol Semantic Views model with it - the roles become its dimensions, facts and metrics; Semantic Views is
installed first when the database does not have it (a publish that fails leaves the approval standing, and says
why). The active workflow's log gets one line.

The work is the kit's own service, setup/lib/describe_service.py in the kit copy (the one `exakit describe` runs),
loaded from its file and run in this process over the kit's connection; without the kit copy, `exakit describe --json` runs as a child process instead.

The role review (role_picker) speaks the five roles of earlier descriptors - entity, category, date, label, text - so
`roles`, `evidence`, `missing` and `set(role, column)` read and write the matching slots: date is the time
slot and label the target.

## nb.describe [#describe]

```python
nb.describe(
    table_or_dataset: str,
    sample: int=SAMPLE,
    *,
    conn=None,
    id: str | None=None,
    force: bool=False,
) -> Draft
```

Describe `SCHEMA.TABLE` (or a dataset id's table): the approved descriptor when the table still matches it,
else a fresh draft. Uses the connection given, else opens the kit's. Only SELECTs run.

## nb.Draft [#Draft]

```python
class nb.Draft
```

A descriptor proposed for a table (status draft), or the approved one describe() returned.

| Member                                                                                          | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `table`                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `version`                                                                                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `status`                                                                                        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `slots`                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `column_roles`                                                                                  |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `roles`                                                                                         | The five roles of earlier descriptors, read from the slots: \{role: column}, \{text: \[column]}.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `evidence`                                                                                      | Per role, the column with its role, confidence and the evidence that chose it, plus the profile's numbers.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `missing`                                                                                       | The roles no column plays, each with the reason the empty slot gives.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `notes`                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `columns() -> list[str]`                                                                        | The table's columns, in table order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `set(role: str \| None=None, column: str \| list[str] \| None=None, **columns: str) -> Draft`   | `set(COLUMN="role", ...)` gives columns a role (one of the eight); `set("label", "COLUMN")`, the form of earlier descriptors, puts a column in that role's slot.                                                                                                                 |
| `slot(**slots: str \| None) -> Draft`                                                           | Put a column in a slot (key, time, text, target, category, entity), or None to leave it empty on purpose.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `assign(role: str, column: str \| list[str] \| None, reason: str \| None=None) -> Draft`        | The role review's correction: `role` (one of the five) to `column`, or empty with `reason`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `copy() -> Draft`                                                                               |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `to_dict() -> dict[str, Any]`                                                                   | The descriptor document (a copy).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `to_yaml() -> str`                                                                              |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `save(path: str \| Path) -> Path`                                                               | Write the descriptor as YAML; exakit_nb.dataset(conn, path) reads it back.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `approve(owner: str \| None=None, comments: bool=True, *, conn=None, sample: int \| None=None)` | Approve: every column has a role and none sits in two slots, the table has not changed since it was profiled, the next version is written into the kit's store with current.yaml, and the schema's Exasol Semantic Views model is rebuilt with it (`comments=False` skips that). |
| `rows() -> list[dict[str, str]]`                                                                | One dict per column, low confidence first: the schema and table it came from, its name, type, role, confidence, evidence and note.                                                                                                                                               |
| `show() -> None`                                                                                | Print each column with its schema and table, type, role, confidence, evidence and note, low confidence first, the slots above.                                                                                                                                                   |


# Approved column maps (/data-scientist/development/reference/descriptor-store)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

Where a user's approved descriptors live. Today: `~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<SCHEMA>.<TABLE>/current.yaml`
(setup/lib/descriptor/store.py writes it; table_descriptor() finds it by its dataset id). Before that, and still read:
`~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/<id>/` (the kit's home, EXAKIT_HOME
when set) holds one `v<n>.yaml` per version and `current`, a text file with the number of the approved version.
Read-only here: `exakit describe <id> --approve` and `Draft.approve()` write versions; `Dataset` reads the
current one before it falls back to a shipped descriptor.

```python
descriptor_store_dir("amazon_sales")   # ~/.exasol-starter-kit/descriptors/amazon_sales
list_versions("amazon_sales")          # [1, 2]: every v<n>.yaml there, in order
current_version("amazon_sales")        # 2, or None when nothing is approved there
current_descriptor("amazon_sales")     # the v2.yaml path, or None
```

## nb.approved_datasets [#approved_datasets]
