```python
nb.approved_datasets() -> list[dict]
```

Every dataset with an approved column map, newest approval first: \{id, table, version, approved_at}.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.column_map_versions [#column_map_versions]

```python
nb.column_map_versions(id: str) -> list[dict]
```

Every saved version of a dataset's column map, oldest first: \{version, approved_at, roles, slots, evidence} -
what approving one of them again (RoleReview\.approve) would restore.

## nb.current_version [#current_version]

```python
nb.current_version(id: str) -> int | None
```

The approved version's number from `current`, or None when there is none (or the file does not hold one).

## nb.descriptor_store_dir [#descriptor_store_dir]

```python
nb.descriptor_store_dir(id: str) -> Path
```

The folder that holds the versions of the descriptor `id` (whether or not it exists yet); an id that is not
a dataset id is refused, so no path is built from it.

## nb.list_versions [#list_versions]

```python
nb.list_versions(id: str) -> list[int]
```

The version numbers stored for `id` (every v\<n>.yaml), ascending; empty when none is stored.


# Documentation (/data-scientist/development/reference/docs)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
nb.docs()                   # the documentation (this notebook's persona section), shown under the cell
nb.docs("descriptor")       # search it for a word
nb.docs(nb.describe)        # one command's page (or nb.docs("describe"))
nb.docs("explore")              # one page, by its address
nb.docs(browser=True)       # in a browser tab instead
```

The documentation is a site of plain files the kit ships (`notebook/docs/site` in the kit copy): pages, styles and
a search index, built ahead of time. This module serves that folder from this Python on this computer only
(the loopback address, a free port) and shows it in a frame under the cell, so reading and searching need no internet, no Node
and no second install. The server starts on the first call and stops with the kernel.

A command's page is found in the site's own list (`commands.json`, written from `exakit.nb`'s `__all__` when the
site is built), so every public helper has one. Anything else is handed to the site's search.

## nb.Docs [#Docs]

```python
class nb.Docs
```

What `nb.docs()` returns: the documentation at `url`. A notebook shows it in a frame under the cell;
`open()` opens it in a browser tab.

| Member           | What it is                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `open() -> Docs` | Open the page in the default browser. |

## nb.docs [#docs]

```python
nb.docs(what: Any=None, *, height: int=640, browser: bool=False) -> Docs
```

Open the notebooks' documentation: all of it, one command's page, one page, or a search.

`what` is nothing (the section of the persona whose notebook this is, else the start page), a helper or its name (`nb.describe`, `"describe"`: that command's page),
a page's address (`"explore"`, `"set-up/ai-and-langfuse"`), or any other words (searched, typos forgiven). The result shows
under the cell in a frame `height` pixels tall; `browser=True` opens a browser tab too. Served from this
computer only, from files the kit ships: nothing is fetched from the internet.


# Hand-off bundle (/data-scientist/development/reference/handoff-bundle)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
bundle = nb.handoff_bundle(connection, dataset)       # ~/.exasol-starter-kit/bundles/<workflow id>/ and .zip
```

The folder holds the approved column map (`descriptor.yaml`), the schema map when there is one
(`schema-map.json`), every query the workflow ran with its digest and row count (`queries.sql`), the workflow log
as it is (`workflow.jsonl`) and a `README.md` that says what the data is, which column map version the numbers rest
on, which questions were approved, which dashboards were published and how to repeat it. Nothing in it is a password:
the log is already written without one, and the connection is the kit's.

This is the Data Scientist's hand-off. The ML Engineer's training handoff (one JSON file with the feature view and the
split, `nb.write_handoff`) is a different thing with its own folder.

## nb.handoff_bundle [#handoff_bundle]

```python
nb.handoff_bundle(
    conn,
    ds: Any,
    workflow_id: str | None=None,
    folder: str | os.PathLike | None=None,
    zip_it: bool=True,
) -> HandoffBundle
```

Write the bundle for `ds` and the workflow (the active one, else the last one on this machine, else none) into
`folder` (default `$EXAKIT_HOME/bundles/<workflow id>/`; a bundle for no workflow is named after the dataset)
and, with `zip_it`, a zip beside it. The active workflow's log gets a `handoff` line with the path.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/03_share`

## nb.HandoffBundle [#HandoffBundle]

```python
class nb.HandoffBundle
```

Where the bundle is and what is in it.

| Member        | What it is  |
| ------------- | ----------- |
| `path`        | `Path`      |
| `zip_path`    | \`Path      | None\` |
| `workflow_id` | \`str       | None\` |
| `files`       | `list[str]` |
| `summary`     | `list[str]` |


# Training handoff (/data-scientist/development/reference/handoff)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

The handoff from the Data Scientist to the ML Engineer (DS-3 -> ML-3, design 4): one JSON file that holds everything
`01_train` needs to train without opening the descriptor - which descriptor version and digest it came from, a digest
of the data, the feature view built from the roles (as `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` SQL), the label and its positive
class, the training SELECT with a reproducible time split, and the input and output schemas. A descriptor without a date
role has no time split: the handoff is refused with the fix (`split="random"` for a reproducible hash split, or a
date role) - a random split is never silent, and `01_train` refuses one the file does not mark as asked for.

```python
path = nb.write_handoff(conn, ds)          # explore's last cell: ~/.exasol-starter-kit/handoffs/<id>-v<n>.json
handoff = nb.read_handoff("amazon_sales")      # the latest one for that descriptor (or a path, or "<id>-v2")
handoff = nb.handoff_from(conn, ds)         # the same record, built from an approved descriptor, not written
nb.handoff_is_stale(conn, handoff, ds)      # None, or the line that says what changed and what to do
```

The feature view is SQL only - category one-hot over the top-20 values plus OTHER, date -> year / month / ISO day of
week / days since the first date, text -> LENGTH, entity -> frequency - so a model that is linear over these columns can
be scored by Rust on the very same view (ML-5): TF-IDF stays out of it (the client-side model in explore keeps it);
top-k token flags computed in SQL are the deferred next step and are recorded as such in the file. The view is not
created here: the ML quickstart and 01_train create it, with the admin profile.

The file names a table, columns, SQL and digests, never a host, a user or a password; the kit's secret-grep test
covers the folder. A workflow that is active gets one `handoff` line in its log (X-1).

## nb.handoff_from [#handoff_from]

```python
nb.handoff_from(
    conn,
    ds: Dataset,
    label: str | None=None,
    split: str | None=None,
    train_share: float=0.8,
    workflow_id: str | None=None,
    written_by: str=WRITTEN_BY,
) -> dict[str, Any]
```

The handoff record for `ds` as design 4 shapes it, built now and returned, nothing written: the descriptor's
id, version, digest (`digest_kind` says whether it is the table digest or the file's) and source; the data
digest (`data_digest_kind`); the feature view; the label and its positive class (`label` overrides it);
the split (`time` over the date role by default; `split="random"` for a hash split, the only way to get one -
without a date role and without that, a ValueError names the fix; `split.explicit` records the choice) and
`train_share`; the training SQL; input and output schemas. `workflow_id` defaults to the active workflow's.

## nb.handoff_is_stale [#handoff_is_stale]

```python
nb.handoff_is_stale(conn, handoff: dict[str, Any], ds: Dataset) -> str | None
```

None when `handoff` still describes `ds` and its data; else the line 01_train prints before it refuses:
the descriptor's version or digest changed (recomputed from `ds`: the same kind the handoff recorded), or - with
a connection - the data digest no longer matches. The fix is in the line.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`

## nb.read_handoff [#read_handoff]

```python
nb.read_handoff(id_or_path: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]
```

The handoff as a dict: from a path to the file, from `<id>-v<n>` (that version's file), or from a descriptor
id (the file with the highest version in the handoffs folder). None there is a FileNotFoundError saying how to
make one.

**Used in:** `ml-engineer/02_rust_score`

## nb.write_handoff [#write_handoff]

```python
nb.write_handoff(
    conn,
    ds: Dataset,
    label: str | None=None,
    split: str | None=None,
    train_share: float=0.8,
    workflow_id: str | None=None,
    written_by: str=WRITTEN_BY,
) -> Path
```

Build the handoff (handoff_from) and write it to `$EXAKIT_HOME/handoffs/<id>-v<n>.json` - the folder 0700,
the file 0600, replaced whole (a temporary file renamed over it) so a reader never sees half of one. The active
workflow's log gets a `handoff` line with the path and the descriptor's id and version. Returns the path.


# All commands (/data-scientist/development/reference)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

Every notebook starts with `import exakit.nb as nb`. Each name below is one call a cell can make, and the same
call a guided card makes behind its buttons.

```python
import exakit.nb as nb
nb.docs(nb.describe)     # open one command's page from a notebook
```

| Command                                                                                                  | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`nb.addon_ready`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-commands#addon_ready)                       | Make an add-on usable from here: install it when it is not (`exakit marketplace <addon>`), start it when it is a service and stopped (`exakit start <addon>`), and say its state and address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.addons`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-facts#addons)                                    | The marketplace's add-ons as `exakit marketplace --list --json` reports them: \{id, name, about, status, installed, version, url}, and `offered`: False for one the kit's catalog does not offer yet (its marketplace/catalog.json says "visible": false, so no marketplace screen lists it).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.ai_clients`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-facts#ai_clients)                            | The AI clients the kit can connect to the database (its MCP adapters), each \{id, name, connected}, with connected from `exakit mcp-status --json`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`nb.approved_datasets`](/data-scientist/development/reference/descriptor-store#approved_datasets)       | Every dataset with an approved column map, newest approval first: \{id, table, version, approved_at}.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`nb.ask`](/data-scientist/development/reference/ask#ask)                                                | Draft SQL from the user's opted-in model endpoint; `proposed_sql` supports manual drafting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`nb.check_bucket`](/data-scientist/development/reference/checks#check_bucket)                           | The deployment's bucket directory exists on this machine where the kit says it is, and - given a connection - a UDF sees it at its /buckets path too (skipped, with a note, when the container check fails).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`nb.check_connection`](/data-scientist/development/reference/quickstart#check_connection)               | The database answers: its time, this session's id and its version, as one row (and one line).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.check_container`](/data-scientist/development/reference/checks#check_container)                     | The container behind `alias` runs a smoke UDF, and it has every package training needs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`nb.check_mlflow`](/data-scientist/development/reference/checks#check_mlflow)                           | Check the destination runs will really use: configured server, kit server, or local store.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.check_model_compatibility`](/data-scientist/development/reference/checks#check_model_compatibility) | Refuse a pickle whose scikit-learn version differs before any scoring SQL runs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`nb.chosen_dataset`](/data-scientist/development/reference/dataset#chosen_dataset)                      | The dataset a notebook works on: `name` when it is set; with None, the one approved last in a quickstart (so picking fraud_transactions there carries on here), else amazon_sales.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`nb.clean_path`](/data-scientist/development/reference/sources#clean_path)                              | A path pasted into a cell, made usable: quotes and spaces around it, a `file://` link, the shell's backslash escapes (`My\ Data`, from a drag into a terminal) and `~` are undone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`nb.column_map_versions`](/data-scientist/development/reference/descriptor-store#column_map_versions)   | Every saved version of a dataset's column map, oldest first: \{version, approved_at, roles, slots, evidence} - what approving one of them again (RoleReview\.approve) would restore.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`nb.components`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-facts#components)                            | The kit's parts as `exakit version --json` reports them: \{id, installed, available, status, add_on, ownership, remedy}, with a status of current, ahead, update_available, available (an add-on not installed) or missing; `available` is the version the kit would install or update to.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.confirm_send`](/data-scientist/development/reference/core#confirm_send)                             | Before sampled rows go to a model endpoint: True at once for a table in the database; for a live source (the descriptor names a source) it names the source and asks, and only a yes sends.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`nb.connect`](/data-scientist/development/reference/core#connect)                                       | A pyexasol connection to the local database, opened from the kit's encrypted store, pinned to the database's TLS certificate once the kit has recorded it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.connect_source`](/data-scientist/development/reference/sources#connect_source)                      | Connect an external source as a virtual schema, from a notebook cell.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`nb.connected_sources`](/data-scientist/development/reference/quickstart#connected_sources)             | The virtual schemas in the database (external sources) with their number of tables; empty when there is none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.connector_inputs`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-facts#connector_inputs)                | What `exakit connect <connector>` asks, from the kit's source engine (`inputs`: what its connect form reads, in the form's order).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`nb.connectors`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-facts#connectors)                            | The kinds of external source `exakit connect` takes, as its own menu lists them (the kit's source engine, `catalog`): \{id, name, summary, aliases, tier, status, version, gate} - `version` the adapter the kit pins, `gate` why one is not available yet (empty when it is).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`nb.continue_workflow`](/data-scientist/development/reference/workflow#continue_workflow)               | The workflow already going, without an id to paste: this kernel's, else the one inherited through EXAKIT_WORKFLOW_ID, else the last one started or resumed on this machine (a quickstart starts one); a new one named `name` only when there is none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`nb.count_name`](/data-scientist/development/reference/readout#count_name)                              | The count column, named after what is counted: ORDER_LINES, STORE_WEEKS; ROW_COUNT when the descriptor does not say (ROWS is an SQL word).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.current_version`](/data-scientist/development/reference/descriptor-store#current_version)           | The approved version's number from `current`, or None when there is none (or the file does not hold one).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`nb.current_workflow`](/data-scientist/development/reference/workflow#current_workflow)                 | The active workflow id: the session's, else the one inherited through EXAKIT_WORKFLOW_ID, else None.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`nb.dash_tools`](/data-scientist/development/reference/dash-mcp#dash_tools)                             | The notebook's Dash Server tool adapter; each call is an MCP tool call.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`nb.DashTools`](/data-scientist/development/reference/dash-mcp#DashTools)                               | Synchronous adapter for notebook cells, which already run an event loop.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`nb.data_checks`](/data-scientist/development/reference/data-checks#data_checks)                        | Prepare: one row per finding - CHECK, COLUMN_NAME, ROWS_AFFECTED, PCT, MEANS - for repeated keys, repeated identifiers, exact copies of a row, empty cells, placeholder values and a rare label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`nb.data_map`](/data-scientist/development/reference/data-map#data_map)                                 | The semantic map of the database: every table by origin (sample, local, source) with its rows, columns, column-map state and roles, then the links between tables - declared, found by an approved schema map, or a shared key-like column name across two tables (marked possible).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`nb.DataMap`](/data-scientist/development/reference/data-map#DataMap)                                   | What data_map found: tables, columns and links, each a list of dicts; DataFrames through the properties.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`nb.Dataset`](/data-scientist/development/reference/dataset#Dataset)                                    | A validated descriptor whose every role the database holds, with the SQL names the notebooks build queries from.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`nb.dataset`](/data-scientist/development/reference/dataset#dataset)                                    | The dataset `name`, checked against the database: a kit dataset id, a descriptor file or its folder, or a data file of your own (CSV, Parquet or JSON) with its descriptor beside it, which is loaded first (load_own_file).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`nb.describe`](/data-scientist/development/reference/describe#describe)                                 | Describe `SCHEMA.TABLE` (or a dataset id's table): the approved descriptor when the table still matches it, else a fresh draft.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`nb.describe_schema`](/data-scientist/development/reference/schema-map#describe_schema)                 | The schema of `dataset_or_schema` (a dataset, or a schema name) as found now: its tables, rows and keys, and every many-to-one link between them with its evidence.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`nb.descriptor_store_dir`](/data-scientist/development/reference/descriptor-store#descriptor_store_dir) | The folder that holds the versions of the descriptor `id` (whether or not it exists yet); an id that is not a dataset id is refused, so no path is built from it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`nb.DescriptorNotApproved`](/data-scientist/development/reference/dataset#DescriptorNotApproved)        | A step that needs an approved descriptor was given a draft; the message says how to approve it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`nb.Docs`](/data-scientist/development/reference/docs#Docs)                                             | What `nb.docs()` returns: the documentation at `url`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`nb.docs`](/data-scientist/development/reference/docs#docs)                                             | Open the notebooks' documentation: all of it, one command's page, one page, or a search.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`nb.Draft`](/data-scientist/development/reference/describe#Draft)                                       | A descriptor proposed for a table (status draft), or the approved one describe() returned.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.draft_question`](/data-scientist/development/reference/question-rules#draft_question)               | A Proposal for `question` drafted by rules from the column map (no AI model): read-only SQL, with the drafter's assumptions, not approved yet.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`nb.effort_levels`](/data-scientist/development/reference/providers#effort_levels)                      | The effort levels this model takes (sent as reasoning_effort); \[] when the provider documents none for it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`nb.exakit`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-commands#exakit)                                 | Run `exakit <args>` and show its output line by line as it comes (`show=False` keeps it quiet); the KitRun says how it ended.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.example_questions`](/data-scientist/development/reference/question-rules#example_questions)         | Up to three questions this dataset's approved roles can answer, in its own column names.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`nb.feature_ideas`](/data-scientist/development/reference/lab#feature_ideas)                            | Feature ideas for this lab's data, each with the SQL that would make it: try one with try_feature.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`nb.find_links`](/data-scientist/development/reference/semantic#find_links)                             | The links between tables of different schemas - sample data, your files, external sources - where no foreign key says so and the names differ, found from the values, each with its evidence (`exakit describe --links`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`nb.first`](/data-scientist/development/reference/quickstart#first)                                     | The first dataset that was loaded, in the order given; says which one is used.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`nb.forget_model`](/data-scientist/development/reference/setup-env#forget_model)                        | Delete what use_model(..., remember=True) saved (the model, Langfuse, or both) and clear it from this kernel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.handoff_bundle`](/data-scientist/development/reference/handoff-bundle#handoff_bundle)               | Write the bundle for `ds` and the workflow (the active one, else the last one on this machine, else none) into `folder` (default `$EXAKIT_HOME/bundles/<workflow id>/`; a bundle for no workflow is named after the dataset) and, with `zip_it`, a zip beside it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`nb.handoff_from`](/data-scientist/development/reference/handoff#handoff_from)                          | The handoff record for `ds` as design 4 shapes it, built now and returned, nothing written: the descriptor's id, version, digest (`digest_kind` says whether it is the table digest or the file's) and source; the data digest (`data_digest_kind`); the feature view; the label and its positive class (`label` overrides it); the split (`time` over the date role by default; `split="random"` for a hash split, the only way to get one - without a date role and without that, a ValueError names the fix; `split.explicit` records the choice) and `train_share`; the training SQL; input and output schemas. |
| [`nb.handoff_is_stale`](/data-scientist/development/reference/handoff#handoff_is_stale)                  | None when `handoff` still describes `ds` and its data; else the line 01_train prints before it refuses: the descriptor's version or digest changed (recomputed from `ds`: the same kind the handoff recorded), or - with a connection - the data digest no longer matches.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.HandoffBundle`](/data-scientist/development/reference/handoff-bundle#HandoffBundle)                 | Where the bundle is and what is in it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| [`nb.kit_check`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-commands#kit_check)                           | The kit as it is now, in a few lines: installed or not, the database, each add-on service and its address, the datasets loaded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`nb.kit_status`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-commands#kit_status)                         | `exakit status --json` as a dict.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`nb.kit_update`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-commands#kit_update)                         | `exakit update` from here (optionally one component: `kit_update("notebook")`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`nb.KitRun`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-commands#KitRun)                                 | One command run: the words it was called with, its exit code and everything it printed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`nb.Lab`](/data-scientist/development/reference/lab#Lab)                                                | One model-lab run: the task, its settings, the data it read and what came out (board and pick for a prediction, groups or unusual rows otherwise).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`nb.lab_data`](/data-scientist/development/reference/lab#lab_data)                                      | The approved data the lab trains on, read once (newest first, at most ROW_LIMIT rows): every usable column, with the ones that give the answer away (nb.leakage_check, unless `leaks` is given) and personal data left out (`.left_out` says why).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`nb.last_workflow`](/data-scientist/development/reference/workflow#last_workflow)                       | The workflow started or resumed last on this machine, when its log is still there; else None.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.leakage_check`](/data-scientist/development/reference/data-checks#leakage_check)                    | Validate: the columns whose values (almost) decide the label on their own - each a value or values where the label is (nearly) always 1 or always 0, covering most rows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`nb.list_schemas`](/data-scientist/development/reference/quickstart#list_schemas)                       | Every schema with its number of tables, virtual ones (connected sources) marked.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| [`nb.list_workflows`](/data-scientist/development/reference/workflow#list_workflows)                     | One summary per log in the workflows folder, oldest first: id, name (from its start line), started, last (first and last timestamps) and events (the line count).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`nb.load_own_file`](/data-scientist/development/reference/own-file#load_own_file)                       | Load your own data and return it as a Dataset the notebooks run on (or a LoadedTable whose roles are reviewed next).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`nb.load_sample`](/data-scientist/development/reference/quickstart#load_sample)                         | A dataset the kit offers (`amazon_sales`, `fraud_transactions`): used as it is when it is loaded, else loaded first with `exakit data-load <id>` (the cell waits for it), then checked against the database.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`nb.load_source`](/data-scientist/development/reference/quickstart#load_source)                         | A table in a connected external source (a virtual schema).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`nb.loaded_files`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-facts#loaded_files)                        | The files `exakit data-load` put into the database, as the kit records them (its load receipts): one row per table, the latest load - \{table, rows, file, loaded_at}.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| [`nb.log_sql`](/data-scientist/development/reference/workflow#log_sql)                                   | Log a statement sql() ran: the session and statement ids that find it in the database's audit log, the statement's SHA-256 (what traces and runs carry), how many rows came back, and the statement text - redacted, with a warning, when it looks credential-bearing (a PASSWORD or API_KEY column, say); this never raises, the query has already run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`nb.model_client`](/data-scientist/development/reference/core#model_client)                             | (client, model ID) for EXAKIT_MODEL_ID and EXAKIT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL; EXAKIT_PROVIDER_API_KEY is optional for servers without authentication.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`nb.model_lab`](/data-scientist/development/reference/lab#model_lab)                                    | Train `task` on the approved dataset: `predict_yes_no` (its target), `predict_number` (`target_number`), `find_groups` or `find_unusual`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`nb.model_list`](/data-scientist/development/reference/checks#model_list)                               | What `exakit model list --json` says: bucket_dir (the host folder), udf_root (the path UDFs read it under) and the models in it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`nb.model_providers`](/data-scientist/development/reference/providers#model_providers)                  | Every provider the notebooks offer: id, name, the Chat Completions address, whether it needs a key ("required", "optional", "none"), where to get one, and whether it runs on this computer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`nb.model_settings`](/data-scientist/development/reference/core#model_settings)                         | Display the chosen model and endpoint without the API key or custom header values; makes no request.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

| [`nb.name`](/data-scientist/development/reference/readout#name)                                          | A result column named after a data column: `CANCELLED` + `PCT` -> `CANCELLED_PCT`; quotes, dots and spaces become underscores, so the name works unquoted in SQL.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

| [`nb.note_trend`](/data-scientist/development/reference/readout#note_trend)                              | Print (and return) the note under a per-period result: the busiest period and the highest and lowest %.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`nb.notebooks`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-facts#notebooks)                              | The kit's notebooks in order (\{id, persona, step, title, summary, file}), from its notebook catalog; only `persona`'s when given.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`nb.noun`](/data-scientist/development/reference/readout#noun)                                          | What a row is, from the descriptor's grain: "one row per order line" -> "order lines" (`one=True`: "order line"), "one row per store and week" -> "store weeks"; at most three words, up to a comma or a word such as "in" or "per"; "rows" when the descriptor does not say.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.persona_plan`](/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-facts#persona_plan)                        | What a persona (this kit's, when not named) brings that is still missing here: `exakit persona plan --json` - \{persona, datasets\{loaded, pending}, addons\{installed, pending, unavailable}, nothing_pending}.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| [`nb.save_descriptor`](/data-scientist/development/reference/own-file#save_descriptor)                   | Write a descriptor document as YAML, in the layout of the kit's own descriptor.yaml files - always as schema_version 2: a schema_version 1 document (or one without the record keys) is written as version 1 with `status` (draft unless the document, or `status`, says approved), the owner (EXAKIT_DESCRIPTOR_OWNER, else the OS user), created now, drafted by the user and, when given, `source` (`file:<path>` for a file's descriptor).                                                                                                                                                                      |

| [`nb.try_feature`](/data-scientist/development/reference/lab#try_feature)                                | Retrain the lab's picked model with `idea` added, on the same split: \{verdict, text, series}.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`nb.typed_view`](/data-scientist/development/reference/prepare#typed_view)                              | The proposal for `ds`'s table: its types, its cleaning and the CREATE VIEW, built from the data and the descriptor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`nb.TypedView`](/data-scientist/development/reference/prepare#TypedView)                                | The proposal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`nb.use_mlflow`](/data-scientist/development/reference/setup-env#use_mlflow)                            | The MLflow server this kernel records runs to: `tracking_uri` (empty: the kit's own MLflow, or what the shell set); `login=True` asks for the server's username and password (hidden).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| [`nb.use_model`](/data-scientist/development/reference/setup-env#use_model)                              | Your model and Langfuse tracing for this kernel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`nb.use_table`](/data-scientist/development/reference/own-file#use_table)                               | A table already in the database, to describe next (review_roles): `SCHEMA.TABLE`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`nb.workflow`](/data-scientist/development/reference/workflow#workflow)                                 | Start a workflow (a new id, a `start` line in its log) or, with `resume`, continue an existing one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`nb.workflow_log`](/data-scientist/development/reference/workflow#workflow_log)                         | Every line of a workflow's log, in order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`nb.write_handoff`](/data-scientist/development/reference/handoff#write_handoff)                        | Build the handoff (handoff_from) and write it to `$EXAKIT_HOME/handoffs/<id>-v<n>.json` - the folder 0700, the file 0600, replaced whole (a temporary file renamed over it) so a reader never sees half of one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |


# Kit commands (/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-commands)



{/* Generated by tools/nb_docs.py from the docstrings in notebook/package/exakit_nb. Edit those, then run the tool. */}

```python
nb.kit_check()                              # what is installed and running, in four lines
nb.exakit("update")                         # any command of the kit; its log streams into the cell
nb.exakit("marketplace", "dash-server")     # install an add-on
nb.addon_ready("dash-server")               # install it if missing, start it if stopped, say where it is
```

Every call runs the same `exakit` the terminal runs (on PATH, else in the kit's bin folder), detached from any
terminal: a question the command would ask takes its default, and a choice is given up front through the variables
the command documents (`nb.exakit("mcp-setup", env={"EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS": "claude"})`). Nothing is read from the
notebook's input. The result says the exit code and keeps the output, so a cell can test `run.ok`.

## nb.addon_ready [#addon_ready]

```python
nb.addon_ready(addon: str, start: bool=True, show: bool=True) -> dict[str, Any]
```

Make an add-on usable from here: install it when it is not (`exakit marketplace <addon>`), start it when it
is a service and stopped (`exakit start <addon>`), and say its state and address. Returns \{addon, installed,
state, url}. An add-on the marketplace does not have is a ValueError; a failed install or start a RuntimeError
(its output was shown).

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`, `data-scientist/03_share`

## nb.exakit [#exakit]

```python
nb.exakit(
    *args: str,
    env: dict[str, str] | None=None,
    show: bool=True,
    timeout: float=TIMEOUT,
) -> KitRun
```

Run `exakit <args>` and show its output line by line as it comes (`show=False` keeps it quiet); the
KitRun says how it ended. A command that takes longer than `timeout` seconds is stopped and says so.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.kit_check [#kit_check]

```python
nb.kit_check(show: bool=True) -> dict[str, Any]
```

The kit as it is now, in a few lines: installed or not, the database, each add-on service and its address, the
datasets loaded. Never raises: without the command it says where it looked. Returns the status document (\{} when
there is none).

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.kit_status [#kit_status]

```python
nb.kit_status() -> dict[str, Any]
```

`exakit status --json` as a dict.

## nb.kit_update [#kit_update]

```python
nb.kit_update(*components: str, show: bool=True) -> KitRun
```

`exakit update` from here (optionally one component: `kit_update("notebook")`). After an update that
touched the notebook helpers, restart this kernel so the new ones load; the line printed says so.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.KitRun [#KitRun]

```python
class nb.KitRun
```

One command run: the words it was called with, its exit code and everything it printed.

| Member      | What it is  |
| ----------- | ----------- |
| `command`   | `list[str]` |
| `code`      | `int`       |
| `output`    | `str`       |
| `timed_out` | `bool`      |
| `ok`        |             |
| `lines`     |             |


# Kit facts (/data-scientist/development/reference/kit-facts)

```python
nb.sample_datasets()          # the kit's sample datasets: id, label, description, schema, loaded

nb.addons()                   # the marketplace's add-ons and their state

nb.notebooks("data-scientist")   # a persona's notebooks, in order
nb.persona_plan()             # what this kit's personas bring that is still missing
```

Nothing here is a list typed into the notebook package: each answer is the kit's own - an `exakit ... --json`
command, or a file of the kit copy these notebooks run with (data/datasets/\*/dataset.conf, notebook/catalog.json,
personas/\*.json, mcp/adapters). The guided view's cards read the same functions, so a card and a cell agree.

## nb.addons [#addons]

```python
nb.addons() -> list[dict[str, Any]]
```

The marketplace's add-ons as `exakit marketplace --list --json` reports them: \{id, name, about, status,
installed, version, url}, and `offered`: False for one the kit's catalog does not offer yet (its
marketplace/catalog.json says "visible": false, so no marketplace screen lists it).

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.ai_clients [#ai_clients]

```python
nb.ai_clients() -> list[dict[str, Any]]
```

The AI clients the kit can connect to the database (its MCP adapters), each \{id, name, connected}, with
connected from `exakit mcp-status --json`.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.components [#components]

```python
nb.components() -> list[dict[str, Any]]
```

The kit's parts as `exakit version --json` reports them: \{id, installed, available, status, add_on,
ownership, remedy}, with a status of current, ahead, update_available, available (an add-on not installed) or
missing; `available` is the version the kit would install or update to.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

## nb.connector_inputs [#connector_inputs]

```python
nb.connector_inputs(connector: str, **settings: Any) -> dict[str, Any]
```

What `exakit connect <connector>` asks, from the kit's source engine (`inputs`: what its connect form reads,
in the form's order). The connector may be named by id or alias. Returns \{id, name, status, gate, name_input,
inputs, forms, access, tips, tree, settings, setting_inputs}: `name_input` is the form's first question (the
source's name); each of `inputs` is \{name, label, kind, required, default, choices, secret, file, hint, prompt,
draft} - `secret` a password or key (never a cell's text), `file` a path to a file, `hint` the lines the form
says above the question. `forms` are the connection-string shapes it reads (`url=`), `access` and `tips`
what its source card says.

A connector with several kinds of source in one (Lakehouse: Iceberg REST, Unity, Glue or a plain folder, on S3 or
Azure) has settings that decide what it asks. `tree` is those settings as the connect menu's tree (a catalog,
and under it the files it can read), each node with the settings its pick gives; give them here
(`connector_inputs("lakehouse", catalog="unity", files="s3")`) and `inputs` are that combination's.
`settings` are the ones in force (given, or the kit's default) and `setting_inputs` the setting questions
themselves, each with its `choices`, their `choice_labels` and the default in force. Every other connector
has an empty `tree` and no `setting_inputs`.

## nb.connectors [#connectors]

```python
nb.connectors() -> list[dict[str, Any]]
```

The kinds of external source `exakit connect` takes, as its own menu lists them (the kit's source engine,
`catalog`): \{id, name, summary, aliases, tier, status, version, gate} - `version` the adapter the kit pins,
`gate` why one is not available yet (empty when it is).

## nb.loaded_files [#loaded_files]

```python
nb.loaded_files() -> list[dict[str, Any]]
```

The files `exakit data-load` put into the database, as the kit records them (its load receipts): one row per
table, the latest load - \{table, rows, file, loaded_at}. A kit dataset (sample_datasets) is not a file here.

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`

`persona`'s when given. `file` is the path under the notebooks folder (starter-kit-notebooks/...).

**Used in:** `data-scientist/00_quickstart`
